faqs.a: Most charters are 3-4 hours. That is enough time to reach the dolphin zones, spend 45-60 minutes with the pods, and stop for a swim. Full-day charters last 6-8 hours and go further out towards the Strait of Gibraltar.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.a: The skipper decides if it is safe to sail. If the sea state is too rough, they will cancel or reschedule. You get a full refund or a new date. Check the forecast before booking. Summer is the safest season for calm seas.

faqs.q: Are children allowed on dolphin charters?
faqs.a: Yes, children are welcome on most boats. Catamarans and motor yachts are best for families because they are stable and have shaded areas. Life jackets for children are provided. Some skippers recommend a minimum age of 4 years for safety.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks?
faqs.a: Yes, most private charters let you bring your own food and drinks. Some include a basic menu of tapas, beer, and soft drinks. Check with the skipper when booking. Glass bottles are not allowed on many boats for safety reasons.

faqs.q: How much does a private dolphin charter cost?
faqs.a: Prices vary by boat type and duration. A half-day RIB charter starts from around EUR 300. A motor yacht from EUR 800. A catamaran from EUR 1,200. Full-day charters cost more. The price includes the skipper, fuel, and basic insurance.

title: Marbella Boat Party Decorations Ideas – Creative Tips
excerpt: Need creative boat party decorations in Marbella? We cover themes, suppliers, and tips for Puerto Banús, Estepona, and beyond. No fluff, just practical ideas.
metaDescription: Creative boat party decorations in Marbella: themes, suppliers, and tips for Puerto Banús, Estepona, and Costa del Sol yachts. Plan your party now.
author: Mardo Soo
content:
The 30-second answer

You want to throw a boat party in Marbella that doesn't look like a sad picnic on a dinghy. The trick is to match your decorations to the boat type, the weather (expect 25-30°C in summer), and the vibe of your departure port. Go for a colour scheme that pops against the Mediterranean blue, use lightweight materials that won't blow away, and hire a local supplier who knows the dock rules. This guide covers themes, where to buy, and what to avoid.

Why boat party decorations in Marbella are different

Decorating a boat in Marbella isn't like decorating a living room or a garden. You are dealing with wind, salt spray, and limited surface area. A motor yacht in Puerto Banús might have a spacious flybridge, but a sailing yacht in Cabopino has a narrow cockpit. You also have to consider that every charter includes a licensed skipper, so the crew will enforce safety rules: no loose items that can fly overboard, no flammable decorations near the engine, and nothing that blocks the life jackets. The good news is that Marbella's climate lets you use light fabrics, balloons, and fresh flowers without worrying about rain. Just avoid heavy paper decorations that turn to mush in the humidity.

Another factor is the departure port. If you are leaving from Puerto Banús, you are competing with superyachts that have professional lighting and floral arrangements. You don't need to match that, but you should at least avoid cheap plastic garlands that scream 'office party'. For Estepona or Sotogrande, a more relaxed, nautical theme works. The key is to plan your decorations around the boat's layout. Talk to your charter company first; they can tell you which areas are safe to decorate and which are off-limits.

Finally, remember that the boat will be moving. Your decorations need to be secured with velcro, clips, or zip ties. Nothing should hang loose enough to catch a breeze and fly into the sea. And please, no glitter. It gets everywhere and the skipper will hate you.

Best themes for a Marbella boat party

Choosing a theme makes your decoration decisions easier. Here are three that work well on the Costa del Sol.

White and gold luxury. This is the classic Marbella look. White tablecloths, gold napkin rings, gold balloons, and white flowers. It works on any boat type, from a 15-metre motor yacht to a catamaran. The white reflects the sun and keeps things cool, while the gold adds a touch of glamour. You can buy gold foil balloons from party shops in Marbella or order online. Just make sure they are filled with air, not helium, because helium balloons can escape and become marine litter.

Nautical chic. Think navy blue, white, and red. Use striped fabrics, rope details, and anchor motifs. This theme is perfect for a sailing yacht or a fishing boat. You can decorate with navy cushions, white bunting, and a few lifebuoy-shaped signs. Avoid anything that looks like a pirate costume. You want to look like you belong on a yacht, not like you are re-enacting 'Treasure Island'.

Tropical fiesta. Bright colours, fake palm leaves, pineapples, and flamingos. This works well for a daytime party on a catamaran or a RIB. The colours look great in photos and match the vibrant atmosphere of Marbella. Use plastic or fabric leaves, not real ones, because real leaves wilt in the heat. Add some LED fairy lights for the evening. Just keep the lights battery-operated and waterproof.

For more inspiration, check out our blog for seasonal party ideas.

Where to buy decorations in Marbella

You have a few options for sourcing decorations in Marbella. The easiest is to buy from a local party shop. There are several in the area, including one near the Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) and another in the centre of Marbella. They stock balloons, bunting, tableware, and themed decorations. Prices are reasonable, though you might pay a premium for last-minute purchases in July and August.

Another option is to order online from a Spanish supplier like Amazon.es or a local florist. Many florists in Marbella offer boat delivery. They can bring flowers, balloons, and even a cake to the dock. Just coordinate with your skipper to make sure the delivery arrives before departure. A typical delivery window is 30 minutes before the charter starts.

If you want something more upmarket, hire an event planner who specialises in yacht parties. They can handle everything from table settings to lighting. Expect to pay from around EUR 500 for a basic setup, more for complex installations. This is worth it if you are hosting a corporate event or a milestone birthday. The planners know the dock rules and can avoid fines from the port authority.

Finally, you can DIY with items from a supermarket like Mercadona or Carrefour. They sell basic party supplies, but you will need to be creative. A pack of colourful napkins and some fairy lights can go a long way. Just remember to bring scissors, tape, and zip ties.

What to avoid when decorating a boat

Mistakes happen, but some are preventable. First, avoid anything that can stain the deck. Red wine is a classic party drink, but it leaves marks on white fibreglass. Use plastic or acrylic wine glasses and stick to white wine or rosé. If you must have red wine, ask the skipper for a designated area with a tablecloth.

Second, do not use candles or open flames. The boat is a confined space with fuel and engines. Even a small candle can be a fire hazard. Use battery-operated LED candles instead. They look just as good and are safe.

Third, avoid heavy decorations that can tip over. A tall centrepiece on a table will topple the first time the boat hits a wave. Keep everything low and stable. Use weighted vases or attach decorations to the table with double-sided tape.

Fourth, do not forget the sun protection. Your decorations should not block the sun or the view. Guests want to see the coast, not a wall of balloons. Keep decorations along the sides or on the table, not in the middle of the deck.

Finally, avoid noise pollution. Marbella has strict noise regulations in ports and near residential areas. Do not bring a loudspeaker or a karaoke machine. The skipper can play music through the boat's sound system at a reasonable volume. If you want a DJ, check with the charter company first.

Tips for specific boat types

Different boats need different approaches. On a motor yacht, you have plenty of flat surfaces and a flybridge. Use the flybridge for a seating area with cushions and a small table. Decorate the main deck with a balloon arch at the entrance. Keep the interior simple because the air conditioning will fight with decorations.

On a catamaran, you have a large trampoline at the front. This is a great spot for a lounging area with throw pillows and a low table. Just make sure the pillows are waterproof or can be stored quickly if the weather changes. The trampoline is also a good place for a photo backdrop. Use a lightweight fabric that won't flap too much in the wind.

Sailing yachts have limited space and a low boom. Do not hang decorations from the boom because it moves when the sails go up. Focus on the cockpit and the table. Use a tablecloth that matches the boat's upholstery. Add a few small vases with flowers. Avoid anything that requires climbing or reaching high.

RIBs and speedboats are small and fast. Decorations need to be minimal. A few balloons tied to the console and some waterproof tableware are enough. Do not try to create a lounge area. The boat is built for speed, not comfort. Keep it simple and focus on the music and the drinks.

Fishing boats are utilitarian. Decorate the cabin with a banner and some bunting. The deck is for fishing gear, not party decorations. If you are hosting a party on a fishing boat, keep the theme casual. A barbecue setup works well here.

How to coordinate with your charter

Before you buy anything, talk to your charter company. They can tell you the exact dimensions of the boat, the layout, and any restrictions. Some charters do not allow decorations at all, especially on superyachts. Others charge a cleaning fee if you leave a mess. Ask about this upfront.

You also need to coordinate the timing. Most charters last 4 hours or a full day. The crew will need time to set up the boat before guests arrive. If you are bringing your own decorations, arrive 30 minutes early. If you are hiring a supplier, confirm the delivery time with the charter company.

Another consideration is the departure port. Puerto Banús has a strict security checkpoint. Your decorations might be inspected. Keep everything in clear bags and avoid anything that looks suspicious. In Estepona, the port is more relaxed, but you still need to follow the rules.

Finally, think about cleanup. You are responsible for removing all decorations at the end of the charter. The crew will not do it for you. Bring garbage bags and make sure nothing goes overboard. Leaving a mess can result in a fine from the port authority.

Common questions

Can I bring my own food and drinks? Yes, most charters allow you to bring your own. But check with the company first. Some have a corkage fee or require you to use their catering service. If you bring your own, use plastic or acrylic cups and plates. Glass is not allowed on most boats.

What if the weather is bad? The skipper decides if the charter goes ahead. If the forecast is bad, you can usually reschedule. For decorations, avoid anything that cannot handle wind or rain. Have a backup plan for indoor spaces.

How much do decorations cost? It varies. A basic balloon setup costs from around EUR 50. A full event planner setup can cost EUR 1,000 or more. For a DIY party, expect to spend EUR 100-200 on supplies from a local shop.

Are there any rules about music? Yes. Keep the volume reasonable. The skipper can control the sound system. Do not bring your own speakers. If you want a specific playlist, send it to the crew in advance.

Can I decorate the outside of the boat? Only if the skipper approves. Do not attach anything to the hull or the railings. Use the deck and the interior only.

What about photos? Decorations make great photo backdrops. Use the bow or the flybridge for group shots. Just be careful not to block the skipper's view. And do not stand on the seats or the table.

Any last tips? Keep it simple. The boat itself is the best decoration. The sea, the mountains, and the sunset are all you really need. A few balloons and some good food will make the party memorable. For more ideas, browse BoatHire24 for inspiration.

Decorating for sunset vs daytime charters

The time of day changes everything about your decoration strategy. For a daytime charter from Cabopino or Marbella Marina, you are fighting the sun. Light colours work best because they reflect heat. White, pastel pink, and light blue keep the deck cooler. Avoid dark fabrics that absorb heat and make guests uncomfortable. For a sunset charter from Puerto Banús, you want warm tones that glow in the golden hour. Copper, rose gold, and amber balloons catch the light beautifully. Add battery-operated fairy lights along the railing. The sunset over La Concha mountain is the real star, so keep decorations low and let the view do the work. For evening charters, invest in LED candles and glow sticks. They are safe, visible, and create a club-like atmosphere without the fire risk. Just remember that summer sunsets in Marbella happen around 21:30 in July, so plan your lighting to come on gradually.

Seasonal decoration ideas for Marbella boat parties

Marbella has distinct seasons that affect what works on a boat. In summer (June to September), temperatures hit 30-35°C. Use water-resistant fabrics and avoid anything that melts. Plastic flamingos and inflatable swans are popular but can be a hazard in wind. Stick to weighted decorations. In spring and autumn (March to May, October to November), the weather is milder at 20-25°C. You can use fresh flowers like roses or sunflowers without them wilting instantly. The sea is calmer, so delicate decorations survive longer. Winter charters (December to February) are rare but possible on sunny days. Focus on warm, cosy decorations like blankets and throw pillows. Use a colour scheme of deep blue and silver to match the winter sea. Avoid anything that looks like Christmas indoors; the boat is already festive enough with the sea views. For New Year's Eve, gold and silver balloons with a countdown banner work well. Just check the port rules for noise after midnight.

Budget-friendly decoration hacks for Marbella boat parties

You do not need to spend a fortune to make a boat party look good. Start with a trip to Mercadona or Carrefour in Marbella. Buy packs of coloured napkins, plastic cups, and a tablecloth for under EUR 20. Use string to create a simple bunting from the napkins. For balloons, buy a balloon pump and a pack of 50 balloons for around EUR 10. Fill them with air, not helium, and tape them to the railing. Another hack is to use fake plants from a Chinese shop like Bazar. A few fake palm leaves in a vase cost EUR 5 and look tropical. For lighting, buy a pack of battery-operated fairy lights from Amazon.es for EUR 8. Wrap them around the table or the steering console. The key is to use colour coordination. Pick two colours and stick to them. Navy and white for nautical, pink and gold for luxury. Avoid mixing too many colours; it looks messy. Finally, use the boat's own features. The white deck is a blank canvas. A few well-placed items go further than a pile of cheap plastic.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own decorations to a boat charter in Marbella?
faqs.a: Yes, most charters allow it. But check with the company first. Some have restrictions on balloons, glitter, or flammable items. Arrive early to set up and bring garbage bags for cleanup.

faqs.q: What decorations work best on a motor yacht?
faqs.a: Lightweight items like balloons, bunting, and tablecloths. Use the flybridge for seating areas. Avoid heavy centrepieces. White and gold themes look great against the blue sea.

faqs.q: Are helium balloons allowed on boats?
faqs.a: Not recommended. Helium balloons can escape and become marine litter. Use air-filled balloons secured with weights or tape. The skipper may ban them entirely.

title: Best Coves for Boat Anchorage in Marbella – Relax
excerpt: Discover the best coves for boat anchorage in Marbella. From Puerto Banús to Estepona, find calm waters, crystal-clear swimming, and sheltered spots. Practical tips on depth, wind protection, and nearby facilities.
metaDescription: Best coves for boat anchorage in Marbella: calm spots, clear water, shelter from wind. Anchor off Puerto Banús, Cabopino, Estepona. Skipper tips included.
author: Mardo Soo
content:
The 30-second answer

The best coves for boat anchorage in Marbella are Cala del Faro (sheltered, sandy bottom, near Estepona), Playa de Cabopino (dunes, clear water, west of Marbella), and the stretch between Puerto Banús and Río Verde (deep water, scenic backdrop of La Concha). All offer calm conditions, good holding, and easy access to swimming. You need a licensed skipper on any charter from BoatHire24, which means you can relax while someone else handles the anchor.

Why anchoring off Marbella works so well

The Costa del Sol coastline runs roughly east-west, so most coves face south or southwest. That gives you shelter from the prevailing Levante wind (east) and Poniente (west). Water depths near the shore range from 3 to 15 metres, with sandy or rocky-sand bottoms that hold a standard Danforth or plough anchor well. Sea temperatures in summer sit around 22-26°C, so you can swim without a wetsuit. Visibility often reaches 10-15 metres on calm days.

Every boat you hire through our search comes with a licensed skipper. That means you don’t need to worry about anchoring technique, local regulations, or reading a chart. The skipper knows the best spots based on wind direction and tide. You just enjoy the swim, the sun, and the view of La Concha mountain.

Anchoring is free in most coves, but you should avoid areas marked with yellow buoys (swimming zones) or near the entrance of marinas. The local authorities are relaxed about day anchoring as long as you don’t block navigation channels or damage seagrass meadows. Keep your distance from other boats, 10 metres minimum, and don’t leave rubbish behind.

Cala del Faro, the hidden gem near Estepona

Cala del Faro sits about 5 nautical miles west of Puerto Banús, just past the Estepona lighthouse. It’s a small cove with a rocky shoreline and a sandy patch in the middle. Depths run from 4 to 8 metres, with a sandy bottom that holds an anchor well. The cove is sheltered from the east wind by a low cliff, so you get calm water even when the Levante blows.

Swimming here is excellent: the water is clear, and there are no jet skis or pedalo hire. You can snorkel around the rocks and see small fish, octopus, and the occasional sea bream. The beach itself is a mix of pebbles and sand, so bring water shoes if you plan to wade ashore. There are no beach bars or restaurants, but you can take a dinghy to Estepona marina (10 minutes) for lunch.

The cove is popular with local boat owners, so arrive by 11 am in July and August. The holding is good in sand, but avoid the patches of seagrass near the rocks. Your skipper will know the exact spot. Depth drops quickly outside the cove, so you can anchor close in and still have 5 metres under the keel.

Playa de Cabopino, dunes, clear water, and space

Playa de Cabopino is a long sandy beach about 8 nautical miles east of Puerto Banús, near the Cabopino marina. The anchorage area is off the western end of the beach, where the seabed is sandy and slopes gently from 3 to 10 metres. It’s one of the few places on this coast where you can anchor in less than 5 metres and still have good holding.

The beach is backed by protected dunes and a pine forest, which means no building or noisy chiringuitos right on the sand. There is a beach bar at the eastern end, but it’s a 15-minute walk. The water is usually calm because the beach faces south and is partly sheltered by the Cabopino headland. On a Poniente day, you might get a slight swell, but it’s rarely uncomfortable.

This is a good spot for families. The water is shallow near the shore, so kids can swim safely. You can take the tender to the beach and spend the afternoon on the sand. The marina at Cabopino has a small supermarket, fuel dock, and a couple of restaurants if you need supplies. Anchoring is free, but don’t block the entrance channel to the marina (marked by green and red buoys).

Puerto Banús to Río Verde, deep water with a view

The stretch of coast between Puerto Banús and the mouth of the Río Verde river is a classic anchorage for motor yachts and catamarans. The seabed is sandy with occasional patches of rock, and depths range from 8 to 20 metres within 200 metres of the shore. You get a stunning backdrop: the white buildings of Puerto Banús, the green valley of Río Verde, and La Concha mountain behind.

This area is exposed to the south and southwest, so it works best on days with light wind or a northerly breeze. On a calm summer morning, the water is flat and clear. You can anchor off the beach of Río Verde (Playa de Río Verde) and swim to the shore. The beach has a couple of restaurants, and you can walk to Puerto Banús in 20 minutes along the promenade.

Holding is generally good in sand, but check the anchor is set because the depth means you have a lot of chain out. A scope of 3:1 to 5:1 is standard. Your skipper will use the engine in reverse to dig the anchor in. This is a popular spot, so expect other boats nearby. Keep a safe distance from the fishing boats that sometimes anchor here overnight.

Playa de la Venus and Playa de la Fontanilla, Marbella town beaches

These two beaches sit right in front of Marbella’s old town, about 3 nautical miles east of Puerto Banús. They are more exposed than the coves further west, but they offer a sandy bottom and depths of 4 to 8 metres. The anchorage is just outside the marked swimming areas (yellow buoys). You can anchor and take the tender to the beach for lunch in the old town.

The water here can be a bit murky because of the sandy seabed and the proximity to the town. But it’s perfectly fine for swimming. The main advantage is convenience: you are minutes from the restaurants, shops, and the Paseo Marítimo. The beaches have chiringuitos where you can get grilled fish and cold drinks.

Wind protection is limited. If the Levante picks up, the swell can build quickly, and you might need to move to a more sheltered spot. Your skipper will monitor the forecast and suggest alternatives. This anchorage works best in the morning before the sea breeze strengthens. By early afternoon, it can get choppy.

Playa de la Cala, west of Marbella, quiet and sandy

Playa de la Cala is a small cove about 2 nautical miles west of Puerto Banús, just past the Hotel Marbella Club. It’s a sandy beach with a rocky headland on the western side. The anchorage is off the beach in 5 to 10 metres of water, with a sandy bottom. The headland gives some shelter from the east wind, so it’s often calmer than the open beaches.

This cove is less crowded than some others because it’s small and there is no beach bar. You can swim to the shore and walk along the coastal path to the next beach. The water is clear, and you might see rays and small fish. It’s a good spot for a quiet afternoon with a book and a cold beer.

Anchoring here requires care because there are a few rocks near the western headland. Your skipper will position the boat in the centre of the cove, away from the rocks. The holding is good in sand, but test it before leaving the boat unattended. Depth drops off quickly outside the cove, so you don’t need to go far from the beach.

Best practices for anchoring in Marbella

Anchoring in the Mediterranean is straightforward if you follow a few rules. Always check the bottom type: sand is best, seagrass is poor, rock is useless. Let out enough chain: a scope of 3:1 in calm conditions, 5:1 if wind is forecast. Set the anchor by reversing gently, then check it with a snorkel or by watching a fixed point on the shore.

In Marbella, the seabed is mostly sand with some seagrass (Posidonia oceanica). Avoid anchoring in seagrass because it damages the ecosystem and your anchor won’t hold. Look for sandy patches, which are usually lighter in colour. Your skipper will know the local spots.

Respect swimming zones marked by yellow buoys. Do not anchor in the approach channels to marinas or near the entrance of Puerto Banús. Keep your distance from other anchored boats, at least 10 metres, more if the wind is strong. And always take your rubbish with you. The coast is beautiful, and everyone wants to keep it that way.

What to bring for a day at anchor

Pack sunscreen (factor 50, water-resistant), a hat, sunglasses, and a rash vest for swimming. Bring snorkelling gear, the visibility is good enough to enjoy the underwater life. A waterproof bag for your phone and keys is useful. Towels, a cooler with drinks and snacks, and a light jumper for the evening breeze.

If you plan to go ashore, bring water shoes for pebble beaches and a small backpack. Some coves have no facilities, so take everything you need. The tender on your charter boat will be a small inflatable with an outboard motor. Your skipper will show you how to use it safely.

Most charter boats have a Bluetooth speaker, so bring your playlist. And a camera or phone with a good zoom for photos of the coast and the mountain. The light in the late afternoon is spectacular, with La Concha turning pink and gold.

Common questions

Do I need a licence to anchor a boat in Marbella?
No, but every boat hired through BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. They handle the anchoring and navigation.

Can I anchor overnight?
Yes, but most coves are exposed to some wind. Cala del Faro and Playa de Cabopino are better for overnight because they offer shelter. Check with your skipper.

Is it safe to swim from an anchored boat?
Yes, as long as the engine is off and the anchor is set. Watch out for other boats and jet skis.

What if the wind picks up?
Your skipper will monitor the forecast and move to a more sheltered spot if needed. There are always alternatives within a few nautical miles.

Can I anchor near Puerto Banús?
Yes, but not in the marina entrance. The area off Playa de Río Verde is fine, but it can be busy. Arrive early for a good spot.

Do I need to pay for anchoring?
No, day anchoring is free in all the coves mentioned. Some beaches have buoys for mooring, but they are usually for local boats.

What depth should I anchor in?
Between 5 and 15 metres is ideal. Shallower than 3 metres risks grounding, deeper than 20 metres requires a lot of chain and may not hold well.

Anchoring with a catamaran, the shallow-draft advantage

Catamarans are a popular choice for day charters on the Costa del Sol because they offer space, stability, and a shallow draft. Most charter catamarans in Marbella draw between 1.2 and 1.8 metres, which means you can anchor closer to the beach than a deep-keel sailing yacht. At Playa de Cabopino, for example, you can get within 30 metres of the shore in 3 metres of water, letting you wade in without a tender. The twin hulls also make the boat more stable at anchor, so you don't get the rolling motion that monohulls suffer in a swell. Your skipper will use two anchors in some coves to keep the boat pointing into the wind, which reduces swinging room and keeps you clear of other boats. If you are looking for a catamaran, try our catamaran search to see options from 32 to 50 feet based in Puerto Banús and Sotogrande.

Motor yachts and the deep-water anchorage off Río Verde

Motor yachts from 40 to 80 feet are the most common charter boats in Marbella, and they handle the deep-water anchorage off Río Verde well. The seabed here drops from 10 to 20 metres within 100 metres of the beach, which suits a motor yacht's deep-V hull. You need at least 40 metres of chain for a 5:1 scope in 8 metres of water, and the windlass on a well-maintained charter boat will handle that without issue. The holding in sand is excellent once the anchor digs in. The view from this spot is the best on the coast: the white facade of the Marbella Club Hotel, the green valley of the Río Verde, and La Concha mountain rising behind. The water depth also means you get cooler, clearer water for swimming. Bring a mask and fins to explore the sandy bottom, where you might see flatfish and the occasional stingray. Most motor yacht charters depart from Puerto Banús, a 10-minute cruise east.

Best season for anchoring, June and September are the sweet spots

July and August are the busiest months on the water in Marbella. The coves fill up by 10 am, and the sea breeze picks up by 2 pm, creating a short chop that can make anchoring uncomfortable on exposed beaches. June and September are better. The water temperature is 22-24°C, which is still warm enough for swimming without a wetsuit. The coves are quieter, with more space between boats. The wind is lighter, often a gentle thermal breeze from the south that dies in the evening. If you are chartering in July or August, book a boat with a departure time before 9 am to secure a good spot. Your skipper will likely recommend Cala del Faro or Playa de la Cala, which are less crowded than the beaches near Puerto Banús. In September, you can anchor at any of the coves mentioned and often have the place to yourself after 5 pm, when the day boats return to port.

Costs, fuel, and what to expect on a day charter

A typical day charter from BoatHire24 includes the boat, skipper, fuel for 4-6 hours of cruising, and basic safety equipment. Fuel costs are usually included in the price for day trips within 10 nautical miles of the departure port. If you want to go further, say to Estepona or Cabopino, there may be a fuel surcharge of around EUR 50-100. Anchoring costs nothing, but you should budget for lunch at a beach club or a chiringuito if you go ashore. A meal for two with drinks at a beach bar near Río Verde costs around EUR 60-80. If you bring your own food and drinks, the boat will have a cooler and a basic galley. Most charter boats also have a Bluetooth speaker and a bimini top for shade. The total cost for a day charter with a skipper starts from around EUR 400 for a RIB or small motorboat, up to EUR 1,500 for a 50-foot catamaran. Check our BoatHire24 homepage for current offers and availability.

Anchoring near Sotogrande, the exclusive alternative

Sotogrande, about 20 nautical miles west of Marbella, offers a different anchoring experience. The coast here is less developed, with long sandy beaches backed by pine forests and low-rise villas. The best anchorage is off Playa de Sotogrande, a 2-kilometre stretch of sand with depths of 5 to 12 metres and a sandy bottom. The holding is good, and the water is often clearer than near Marbella because there is less river runoff. The main advantage is space: even in August, you can find a spot with 50 metres of clear water around you. The downside is that there are fewer beach bars and facilities. You can take the tender to the Sotogrande marina, which has a supermarket, restaurants, and a fuel dock. The marina is about 1 kilometre from the beach, so it is a short walk. If you want a quiet day away from the crowds, Sotogrande is worth the extra cruising time. Departure from Puerto Banús takes about 45 minutes at 20 knots.

What to do if the anchor drags, a practical guide

An anchor can drag if the wind shifts, the bottom is poor, or you did not let out enough chain. In Marbella, the most common cause is a sudden increase in the Levante wind, which can gust to 20 knots in minutes. If you feel the boat moving sideways or the anchor chain vibrating, your skipper will take immediate action. The first step is to start the engine and motor forward gently to take the load off the anchor. Then retrieve the anchor and move to a new spot. If the wind is strong, your skipper will use the engine to hold position while the anchor is brought up. Do not try to reset the anchor in the same spot. Look for a patch of sand away from seagrass. A scope of 5:1 is the minimum in windy conditions. If the wind is forecast to exceed 20 knots, it is safer to head back to port or find a sheltered cove like Cala del Faro, where the cliffs break the wind. Your skipper has local knowledge and will not take risks.

faqs.a: Yes, but most coves are exposed to some wind. Cala del Faro and Playa de Cabopino are better for overnight because they offer shelter. Check with your skipper.

faqs.a: Yes, as long as the engine is off and the anchor is set. Watch out for other boats and jet skis.

title: Stag Do Boat Activities in Marbella – Fun Ideas
excerpt: Stag do boat activities in Marbella: from jet skiing and paddleboarding to DJ boat parties and sunset cruises. Practical tips for a male-only charter on the Costa del Sol.
metaDescription: Plan the ultimate stag do boat activities in Marbella. Jet skiing, DJ parties, sunset cruises, and more. Find your charter with a skipper on BoatHire24.
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

For a stag do in Marbella, a private boat charter offers the best mix of sun, sea, and partying without the hangover of a club queue. You can rent a 12-metre motor yacht for around EUR 1,500 for a half day, which includes a skipper, fuel, and basic water toys. Activities range from jet skiing and inflatable banana rides to DJ decks and sunset champagne sessions. The key is choosing a boat with enough deck space for your group and a skipper who knows the best coves for swimming. Book early, especially in July and August.

Why a boat charter works for a stag do

Marbella in summer hits 32 degrees C, and the last thing you want is a sweaty bar crawl. A boat gives you your own floating VIP area. You control the music, the drinks, and the itinerary. No dress code, no queue, no last orders. The skipper handles the navigation so you can focus on the groom. Most charters depart from Puerto Banús, which is a 10-minute taxi from Marbella centre. You can anchor near the sandbank off Puerto Banús for waist-deep water and bring your own coolbox. Just remember: glass bottles are banned on most boats, so bring plastic cups.

Top stag do boat activities in Marbella

  • Jet ski hire: Many charters offer a towed jet ski as an add-on. Expect to pay around EUR 100 for 30 minutes. The skipper will brief you on the safety zone near the coast.
  • Inflatable towables: A banana boat or donut for up to 6 people. Hilarious when someone falls off in slow motion. About EUR 80 for 15 minutes.
  • Snorkelling and paddleboarding: The water clarity around Cabopino is decent. SUP boards are usually free with the charter.
  • DJ deck and sound system: Some yachts come with a built-in DJ setup. You can also bring a Bluetooth speaker, but the boat's system will be louder.
  • Sunset cruise with cava: The classic. Sail west from Marbella towards Estepona as the sun drops behind La Concha mountain.

For a full list of boats with these features, check out BoatHire24 and filter by water toys or sound system.

Choosing the right boat for a male group

Not all boats are stag-friendly. A 10-metre sailing yacht might look classy but has limited deck space and a low boom that will knock you out if you stand up quickly. For a group of 8 to 12, go for a 12- to 15-metre motor yacht with a large aft deck and a sunpad area. Catamarans are also solid because they don't heel and have a wide beam, meaning more room for dancing. RIBs are fine for a high-speed thrill but not for lounging. Always ask the skipper if the boat has a toilet and a freshwater shower. You will need both after a few beers and a swim.

Itinerary ideas for a half-day or full-day charter

DurationRouteActivities
Half day (4 hours)Puerto Banús to Cala del FaroSwim stop, jet ski, paddleboard, lunch at a chiringuito
Full day (8 hours)Marbella to EsteponaSnorkel at Cabopino, dolphin watching off Gibraltar, sunset cava

For a half day, you can leave at 11am, anchor for lunch at 1pm, and be back by 3pm. That gives you time for a siesta before the evening. Full-day charters often include a stop at a beach club for lunch, but that adds cost. Most skippers will recommend a route based on the wind and swell. The Strait of Gibraltar can get choppy in the afternoon, so morning crossings are better for spotting dolphins.

What to bring and what to avoid

Bring a waterproof Bluetooth speaker, a cooler with drinks and ice, plenty of suncream (SPF 50), sunglasses with a strap, and a towel. Avoid glass bottles, red wine (stains the deck), and anyone who gets seasick easily. If the groom is prone to motion sickness, give them a seasickness tablet an hour before departure. Also, bring a spare pair of shorts in case someone falls in fully clothed. Most skippers provide life jackets, but check that they have enough for your group size.

Costs and booking tips

Prices vary wildly. A basic 8-metre RIB for 6 people starts from around EUR 600 for a half day. A 15-metre motor yacht for 12 people costs from EUR 2,500. Always confirm what is included: fuel, skipper, water toys, and cleaning fees. Some companies add a 20% service charge for large groups. Book at least two weeks ahead for July and August. Use BoatHire24's search to compare boats and read the fine print on cancellation policies. A 50% deposit is standard, with the balance due on the day.

Legal and safety stuff

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper, so you don't need a boating licence. The skipper has the final say on safety. If the sea state is too rough, they may cancel or reroute. Alcohol is allowed on board, but the skipper cannot drink. If anyone in your group is visibly drunk and causing a risk, the skipper can terminate the trip early. Life jackets must be worn during water sports. Also, note that anchoring is prohibited in certain protected areas like the Cabopino dunes. Your skipper will know the no-go zones.

Common questions

Can we bring our own DJ or music? Yes. Most boats have a Bluetooth or auxiliary input for your phone. Some luxury yachts have a built-in DJ booth you can use. Just keep the volume reasonable so you don't annoy other boats.

What if the weather is bad? The skipper will decide. If the trip is cancelled due to weather, you get a full refund or can reschedule. If you cancel on the day, you may lose your deposit.

Is there a minimum age? You must be 18 or over to charter a boat. Some operators allow 16-year-olds with parental consent, but for a stag do, everyone should be legal drinking age.

Can we stop at a beach club? Yes, but you need to book a table in advance. Popular spots include Nikki Beach and Ocean Club. The skipper can drop you off at the jetty and pick you up later.

How many people can fit on a boat? It depends on the boat's licence. A typical 12-metre motor yacht is certified for 12 passengers plus the skipper. Overcrowding is a safety violation, so don't try to sneak extra guests.

Do we need to tip the skipper? It is not mandatory but appreciated. 10% of the charter fee is standard if the service was good.

Can we fish? Some boats have fishing rods. You need a fishing licence for certain species. Ask your skipper if it is possible, and whether they can arrange a licence for the day.

Why Puerto Banús is the ideal departure point for a stag do

Puerto Banús is the natural starting point for any stag do boat adventure. The marina is lined with superyachts, designer shops, and bars that spill onto the boardwalk. You can meet your skipper at the fuel dock near the Casino Marbella at 10am, board your charter, and be sipping a beer within five minutes. The marina has paid parking for EUR 3 per hour, or you can get a taxi from Marbella centre for around EUR 15. If you want a pre-boat breakfast, head to La Pesquera on the port for fried fish and a cold beer. The energy here sets the tone for the day, and you will see other stag groups doing exactly the same thing.

Best motor yachts for a stag group of 10 to 14 people

For a group of 10 to 14, you want a motor yacht between 12 and 15 metres. The Azimut 55 is a popular choice, with a large cockpit seating area, a sunpad on the bow, and a decent sound system. Expect to pay from around EUR 2,200 for a half day. Another solid option is the Sunseeker Portofino 53, which has a more open-plan layout and a wet bar. If you want something with a bit more deck space for dancing, look at a Beneteau Gran Turismo 50. These boats usually come with a Bluetooth stereo, a fridge for drinks, and a small cabin with a toilet. Always ask the charter company whether the boat has a bimini top for shade, because eight hours of direct sun will ruin anyone.

How to book a jet ski or water toys as an add-on

Most motor yacht charters in Marbella offer water toys as an optional extra. Jet skis are the most popular. You can rent a single jet ski for around EUR 100 for 30 minutes, or a double for EUR 150. The skipper will tow the jet ski behind the yacht, so you can use it at the anchor spot. For inflatable towables like a banana or donut, expect to pay EUR 80 for 15 minutes. Some operators bundle water toys into the charter price, so ask when you book. If you want a Seabob, those cost around EUR 200 for 30 minutes. Be aware that water toys are weather-dependent. If the sea state is Force 4 or above, the skipper may refuse to deploy them for safety reasons.

Best time of year for a stag do boat trip in Marbella

The peak season is July and August, when temperatures hit 32 degrees C and the sea is around 24 degrees C. This is also when prices are highest and availability is tight. For a better balance of weather and cost, aim for June or September. June has long days and the water is warm enough for swimming. September is still hot, but the crowds thin out after the first week. May and October are cooler at around 24 degrees C, but you can still get a good day on the water if the sun is out. Avoid November to March unless you are after a very cheap charter and don't mind cold winds. The best time to spot dolphins is from April to June, when they migrate through the Strait of Gibraltar.

What to do if someone gets seasick on the boat

Seasickness can hit even the hardiest stag member, especially if the boat is anchored in a swell. The best prevention is to take a seasickness tablet like Dramamine or Kwells an hour before departure. Ginger ale and dry crackers also help. If someone does feel sick, get them to the centre of the boat, keep them hydrated, and have them look at the horizon. Avoid sending them below deck, as the enclosed space makes it worse. Most skippers carry sick bags, but bring your own just in case. If the groom is the one who gets sick, the day is effectively over, so make sure he takes the tablet.

How to handle the evening after a boat charter

After a day on the water, the natural move is to head to a beach club or a bar near Puerto Banús. You will be back at the marina by 3pm for a half-day charter, or 6pm for a full day. Shower at the marina's public facilities (EUR 2) or at your accommodation, then head to La Sala for a pre-dinner drink. For dinner, try El Pescador for seafood or La Moraga for tapas. If you want to keep the party going, Pangea or Olivia's are the main clubs in Puerto Banús. Avoid booking a table at a club before you know your return time, because boat trips can run late if the wind picks up. Most clubs have a EUR 30 to EUR 50 cover charge for stag groups, so factor that into your budget.

What to do if the weather turns bad on the day

Marbella's weather is generally reliable, but the sea can change quickly, especially in the afternoon when the Levante wind picks up. If the skipper decides the conditions are unsafe, they will either cancel the trip or offer an alternative route closer to the coast. You should get a full refund if the cancellation is weather-related, but check the charter's policy before booking. If you are already on the water and the wind increases, the skipper may head to a sheltered cove like Cala del Faro or the lee side of Cabopino. Do not argue with the skipper's decision. They have the final say on safety, and a rough sea is no fun for anyone.

How to split costs and handle deposits for a stag group

Stag groups often struggle with collecting money from everyone. The easiest method is to have one person pay the full deposit (usually 50 per cent) and then collect from the others via a group payment app like Revolut or Splitwise. The balance is due in cash on the day, so make sure someone is responsible for that. If someone drops out at the last minute, you may lose their share unless you have a backup. Some charter companies allow you to reduce the guest count up to 48 hours before departure, but you still pay for the boat, not per person. Always confirm the cancellation policy in writing. A common trap is the "cleaning fee" for stag groups, which can be EUR 100 to EUR 200 if the boat is left messy.

Why you should consider a catamaran for a larger stag group

If your stag group is 16 to 20 people, a catamaran is a better choice than a motor yacht. Cats have a wide beam, so they don't heel, and they offer more deck space for the same length. A Lagoon 42 or Bali 4.6 can comfortably hold 18 guests. The downside is speed: a catamaran cruises at around 8 knots, compared to 20 knots for a motor yacht. That means you spend more time getting to the anchor spot. But for a full-day charter, that is not a problem. Catamarans also have a shallow draft, so you can anchor closer to the beach. Prices for a 14-metre catamaran start from around EUR 2,800 for a half day. Check the boat's sound system, because some cats have a poor layout for music.

How to find a skipper who is good with stag groups

Not every skipper enjoys taking stag groups. Some prefer quiet couples or families. When you book through BoatHire24, you can read the skipper's profile and see if they mention "groups" or "parties". A good stag skipper will be relaxed about music volume, let you bring your own drinks, and know the best spots for water sports. They will also be clear about the rules: no glass, no jumping off the flybridge, and no swimming in the marina. If you want a skipper who will join in the banter, look for one with a few years of charter experience. Avoid skippers who are new or who seem nervous. A stressed skipper makes for a tense day.

title: Marbella Boat Trip for Sunset Champagne – Romantic
excerpt: A sunset champagne boat trip in Marbella is the ultimate romantic experience. Charter a private yacht from Puerto Banús, sip bubbly as the sun dips behind La Concha, and cruise the Costa del Sol coastline. Prices from around EUR 500.
metaDescription: Book a sunset champagne boat trip Marbella. Private yacht charter from Puerto Banús with bubbly, skipper, and stunning views. Romantic evening on the Costa del
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

A sunset champagne boat trip in Marbella is exactly what it sounds like: you, a private yacht, a chilled bottle of bubbly, and the sky doing its best impression of a postcard. You depart from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina, cruise past the golden beaches and the Sierra Blanca foothills, and anchor somewhere quiet as the sun drops behind La Concha mountain. Most charters include a licensed skipper, so you don't need a licence or any sailing experience. Prices start from around EUR 500 for a two-hour evening cruise on a motor yacht, and go up to a few thousand for a superyacht with a crew. You can book through BoatHire24 and have the whole thing sorted in a few clicks.

Why Marbella works for a sunset champagne trip

Marbella sits on the southwest coast of Spain, which means the sun sets over the sea. That sounds obvious, but it is not the case everywhere on the Costa del Sol. In Nerja or the eastern side of Málaga, the sun drops behind the mountains, not the water. Here, you get a clear horizon line. The sky turns that deep orange and pink for a good 45 minutes, and the light hits the whitewashed buildings of Puerto Banús in a way that makes even the most cynical person reach for their phone camera.

The geography helps too. The Sierra Blanca and La Concha mountain create a natural backdrop that reflects the sunset colours. As you cruise west, you pass the Cala del Faro, a small cove with a lighthouse that looks like it was designed for Instagram. Further out, the Strait of Gibraltar can be visible on a clear day, and sometimes you spot dolphins. The water temperature in summer is around 24 degrees C, so you can actually swim if you anchor in a quiet spot. If you want a more detailed look at the area, the BoatHire24 blog has guides on the best departure ports and routes.

The whole experience is designed for two people, but you can also bring a small group. Most boats on the platform have a maximum capacity of 10 to 12 guests, but for a romantic evening, you want it to be just the two of you. The skipper stays up front and gives you privacy. You bring the champagne, or you can ask the charter company to provide it. Some boats have a cooler, a sound system, and even a small cabin if you want to freshen up.

Which boat to choose for a sunset champagne trip

You have options. The most popular choice for a romantic evening is a motor yacht between 35 and 50 feet. Something like a 40-foot Azimut or a 42-foot Sunseeker. These boats have a large aft deck with a seating area where you can sit and watch the sunset, a bow with sun pads, and a cabin below deck with a toilet and a small galley. They cruise at around 20 knots, so you can cover a decent stretch of coastline in two hours.

Catamarans are another option. They are more stable, so if you or your partner gets seasick, a catamaran is the safer bet. The deck space is larger, and you can set up a table with the champagne and some tapas. A 40-foot Lagoon catamaran has a flybridge with a panoramic view, which is great for sunset. The downside is that catamarans are slower, around 8 to 10 knots, so you cover less distance. But for a sunset trip, that is not a problem. You are not trying to get anywhere fast.

For the full romantic cliché, you could charter a sailing yacht. There is something about the silence of the sails and the sound of the water that makes the champagne taste better. A 38-foot Bavaria or a 40-foot Dufour will do the job. The skipper handles the sails, and you just sit back. The main trade-off is that sailing yachts heeling angle can make pouring champagne tricky. If you go for a sailboat, make sure the skipper motors rather than sails during the champagne part.

If you want to go all out, there are superyachts available in Puerto Banús. A 70-foot Sunseeker or a 90-foot Ferretti will set you back a few thousand euros for a few hours, but you get a crew, a jacuzzi, and a level of service that makes you feel like a Bond villain. You can browse all the options on the BoatHire24 search page and filter by boat type, price, and departure port.

What time to go and how long the trip lasts

Sunset in Marbella varies by season. In summer, the sun sets around 9:30 PM to 9:45 PM. In winter, it is closer to 6:00 PM. You want to be on the water at least 30 minutes before sunset, so you have time to get to a good spot, anchor, and settle in. Most charters offer a two-hour slot that covers the golden hour and the actual sunset. If you want to see the stars come out and the lights of Puerto Banús reflect on the water, book a three-hour slot.

The typical itinerary goes like this. You meet at the marina at the agreed time. The skipper gives a quick safety briefing and helps you onboard. You motor out of the harbour, past the superyachts and the restaurants. Once you clear the breakwater, the skipper opens up the throttle and you cruise west along the coast. You pass the Marbella Marina, the Rio Verde, and the residential towers of San Pedro de Alcántara. The skipper finds a quiet spot near the Cala del Faro or just off the coast of Estepona. He drops the anchor, and you have your sunset moment. On the way back, you cruise past the lit-up marina and dock.

If you want to combine the sunset with a dinner, some charters offer a three-hour option that includes anchoring for a swim and then heading to a beach club or restaurant. You can also arrange for a private chef to come onboard and prepare a meal. That costs extra, obviously, but it is an option.

What to bring and what to expect

Bring the champagne. Or cava, if you want to keep it Spanish. Most boats have a cooler with ice, so you can chill it onboard. You can also bring a bottle of wine, some beer, or soft drinks. The skipper will provide water. Some charter companies offer a champagne package with a bottle of Moët or Veuve Clicquot and a fruit platter. Check the listing on BoatHire24 to see what is included.

Bring a jacket or a light sweater. Even in summer, the sea breeze can get chilly once the sun goes down. The temperature can drop by 5 to 8 degrees C in an hour. Wear non-slip shoes, or take them off and go barefoot. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still useful until the sun sets. A camera or phone with a good camera is essential. The light in the last 20 minutes before sunset is ridiculous.

Do not expect to go fast. The skipper will cruise at a relaxed pace. This is not a speedboat trip. If you want thrills, book a RIB for a different occasion. This is about sitting still and watching the sky change colour. The skipper will stay out of your way, but he is there for safety. You can ask him to take a photo of you both. He has done it a hundred times before.

Which departure port to choose

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice. It is the most glamorous marina on the Costa del Sol, with the superyachts, the designer shops, and the restaurants. You can walk from the port to the yacht in five minutes. The sunset views from here are excellent because you are facing west, and you can see the coast all the way to Gibraltar on a clear day.

Marbella Marina, also called Puerto Deportivo, is smaller and quieter. It is closer to the old town, so you can combine the boat trip with a walk through the orange-tree-lined streets and a dinner at a traditional tapas bar. The marina is less crowded, and parking is easier.

Cabopino is a tiny marina near the dunes of Artola. It is more rustic and less flashy. If you want a low-key, private vibe, this is the place. The beach nearby is one of the least developed on the coast. Estepona is further west, and the marina there is modern and well-equipped. From Estepona, you can cruise towards the Strait of Gibraltar and see dolphins. Sotogrande is the most exclusive, with a polo club and a golf course. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, closer to Málaga airport, and has a large marina with many boat options.

Each port has its own character. For a romantic sunset champagne trip, Puerto Banús or Estepona are the best bets. You can find boats available at each port on the BoatHire24 search page.

How to book and what it costs

Booking is straightforward. Go to BoatHire24, enter Marbella as the destination, select the date and time, and filter by boat type. You will see a list of available boats with photos, descriptions, and prices. The price for a two-hour sunset cruise on a motor yacht starts from around EUR 500 for two people. That includes the skipper, fuel, and the boat. Champagne is extra, unless the listing says it is included. For a catamaran, expect EUR 600 to EUR 900. For a sailing yacht, EUR 400 to EUR 700. For a superyacht, price on request, but start at a few thousand.

Some charter companies offer a sunset package that includes a bottle of cava and a fruit platter. Others let you bring your own. Read the listing carefully. You can also request a specific skipper or a female skipper if that matters to you. The booking system is secure, and you pay online. Cancellation policies vary, but most offer a full refund if you cancel 48 hours in advance.

If you want to book a group trip for a birthday or an anniversary, you can contact the charter company directly through the platform. They can arrange decorations, a cake, or a photographer. Just ask.

Common questions

Do I need a boat licence? No. All charters on BoatHire24 include a licensed skipper who handles the boat.

Can I swim during the sunset trip? Yes, if the skipper anchors in a safe spot. Most trips include a swim stop if the weather is calm.

Is the champagne included? Not always. Check the listing. Some boats offer a champagne package, others let you bring your own.

What happens if the weather is bad? The skipper will cancel or reschedule. You get a full refund or a credit.

Can I bring food? Yes. Most boats have a cooler and a table. You can bring tapas, sushi, or a picnic.

How many people can come? Most boats have a maximum of 10 to 12 guests. For a romantic trip, it is usually just two.

What time should I arrive at the marina? 15 minutes before the scheduled departure. The skipper will meet you at the dock.

How the season affects your sunset champagne trip

Summer is the obvious choice, but it is not the only one. From June to September, the sun sets late and the sea is warm. You can swim before the champagne, and the evenings are long. The downside is that Puerto Banús is packed, and you will share the water with other boats. The best anchor spots near Cala del Faro can have five or six boats at the same time. If you want solitude, go in May or October. The sunset is earlier, around 8:30 PM, and the temperature is still pleasant at 22 to 25 degrees C. The water is cooler, around 18 degrees, but you can still swim if you are brave. The light in October is softer, and the crowds are gone. In winter, the sun sets by 6:00 PM, and the temperature drops to 15 degrees. It is still possible, but you need a jacket and a blanket. Some boats have a heated cabin. Check the listing on BoatHire24 for boats with enclosed saloons if you are booking outside summer.

Where to anchor for the best sunset views

The Cala del Faro is the most popular spot, and for good reason. It is a small cove west of Puerto Banús with a lighthouse on the cliff. The water is calm, and the view of the sun setting behind the lighthouse is iconic. But it can get busy. A quieter alternative is the bay off Estepona, near the marina. You get a wide horizon and the Sierra Bermeja mountains in the background. Another option is the area off the dunes of Artola, near Cabopino. There are no buildings, just sand and pine trees. The sunset here feels more natural. If you want to see Gibraltar in the distance, head towards the Strait of Gibraltar. On a clear day, you can see the Rock and even the coast of Africa. The skipper will know the best spots based on the wind and the tide. You can also ask to anchor near the Rio Verde estuary, where the river meets the sea. It is shallow and quiet, and the birds come out at dusk.

What champagne to bring and how to serve it

You do not need to bring a vintage Dom Pérignon. A good Spanish cava, like a Reserva from Freixenet or a Corpinnat from Gramona, costs around EUR 15 to EUR 25 and tastes excellent. If you want champagne, a bottle of Moët & Chandon Impérial or Veuve Clicquot Yellow Label is around EUR 40 to EUR 50 in a Spanish supermarket. Bring two bottles. One for the sunset, one for the cruise back. Chill them in the boat's cooler for at least an hour before serving. Most boats have plastic flutes, but you can bring your own glassware if you want to be fancy. Wrap the stems in napkins to stop them from clinking. Serve the champagne with a small bowl of salted almonds or olives. The salt cuts through the bubbles and makes the whole thing feel more deliberate. If you want to go full Spanish, bring a bottle of manzanilla sherry instead. It is dry, salty, and pairs perfectly with the sea air.

title: Marbella Boat Party Catering Ideas – Delicious Menu
excerpt: Planning a boat party in Marbella? We cover catering ideas from tapas to paella, plus tips on drinks, dietary needs, and hiring a private chef for your charter.
metaDescription: Discover the best boat party catering ideas for Marbella. From tapas to paella, we help you plan a delicious menu for your yacht charter. Book your boat today.
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

For a boat party in Marbella, the best catering options are easy-to-eat finger foods like Spanish tapas, fresh seafood platters, and portable paella. You want dishes that work well on a moving deck and don't require much fuss. Most charters let you bring your own catering, or you can hire a private chef through the skipper. Keep drinks simple: cava, beer, and non-alcoholic options to avoid seasickness. Plan for about EUR 30-50 per person for a decent spread, excluding drinks.

Why catering matters on a boat party

You are on a boat, not a restaurant. The wind, the sun, and the gentle (or not so gentle) rocking all affect what you can serve. Nobody wants to chase a runaway olive across the deck or deal with a sauce that ends up on your white linen trousers. The key is to pick foods that stay put: skewers, wraps, and bite-sized portions. Think of it as a floating picnic with a bit more style.

Marbella's culinary scene is a natural fit for boat parties. You have access to top-quality seafood from the Mediterranean, local cheeses, and cured meats. The climate means you can serve cold dishes without worrying about them spoiling too quickly, but you still need a cool bag or the boat's fridge. Most yachts have a small galley, but don't expect a full kitchen. That is where pre-prepared catering shines.

If you charter through BoatHire24, the skipper can often recommend local caterers who specialise in boat deliveries. They know the drill: arrive at the dock on time, pack everything in disposable or reusable containers, and provide disposable plates and cutlery. No one wants to wash up on holiday. You can also ask about hiring a private chef for the day, which adds a touch of luxury without the stress.

Top menu ideas for your Marbella boat party

Here are some crowd-pleasing options that work well on the water. You can mix and match based on your group size and budget.

  • Spanish tapas platter: Think patatas bravas (cold version), jamón ibérico, manchego cheese, olives, and piquillo peppers. Easy to share and no cutlery needed. Cost from around EUR 15 per person.
  • Seafood feast: Grilled prawns, octopus salad, mussels in escabeche, and a whole sea bass ceviche. Fresh and light. Allow EUR 25-35 per person.
  • Paella to go: Many restaurants in Puerto Banús do takeaway paella in foil trays. Seafood or mixed paella works best. Serve it in small bowls. Around EUR 12-18 per person.
  • Gourmet sandwiches: Use crusty bread or baguettes with fillings like roasted vegetables, Serrano ham, and brie. Cut into halves for easy handling. About EUR 10 per person.
  • Dessert bites: Churros with chocolate dip (keep the chocolate in a thermos), mini flans, or fresh fruit skewers. Sweet but not heavy.

For drinks, stick to cava (Spanish sparkling wine), beer, and plenty of water. Avoid red wine unless you want stains on the deck. And remember: alcohol hits harder on the water, so pace yourself. You can find more tips on our blog about staying safe while partying at sea.

Dietary requirements and allergies

Boat parties often have a mix of guests, so you need to cater for everyone. The good news is that Mediterranean cuisine is naturally accommodating. For vegetarians and vegans, tapas like patatas bravas, gazpacho, and grilled vegetables are easy. For gluten-free, avoid bread and opt for rice-based dishes like paella or quinoa salads. Many local caterers in Marbella are used to requests for halal or kosher options, but you need to order in advance.

One tip: always ask your guests about allergies before you order. Common triggers on boats include shellfish (prawns, mussels) and nuts (often in pesto or sauces). If someone has a severe allergy, consider a separate menu for them. The skipper should also be informed in case of an emergency. Most charter companies have a first aid kit, but you cannot rely on it for anaphylaxis.

If you are unsure, a simple buffet of separate ingredients (cheese, meats, bread, salads) lets everyone build their own plate. That way, you avoid cross-contamination. You can also find boats on BoatHire24 with a galley that allows for some food prep, which gives you more flexibility.

Where to source catering in Marbella

You have several options for getting food onto your charter boat. The easiest is to order from a local restaurant that offers delivery to the marina. Many places in Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina have boat-friendly takeaway menus. Expect to pay a small delivery fee, usually around EUR 10-20, depending on the distance. Popular spots include La Pesquera for seafood and El Pescador for tapas.

Another option is to hire a private catering company that specialises in yacht charters. These companies handle everything from menu planning to setting up the table on the boat. Prices vary, but you can expect from EUR 40-80 per person for a full service. Some even provide a server for the day. This is a good choice if you want a more formal party or have a large group.

Finally, you can DIY. Stop at a supermarket like Mercadona or Carrefour in Marbella before you board. Grab pre-made salads, cured meats, cheese, bread, and drinks. It is cheaper and gives you control over the menu. Just remember to bring ice and cool bags. The boat's fridge is usually small, so plan accordingly.

Drinks and hydration tips

On a sunny Marbella day, you will be thirsty. The combination of sun, wind, and alcohol can dehydrate you quickly. A good rule is to have one non-alcoholic drink for every alcoholic one. Water is essential, but you can also bring flavoured sparkling water, iced tea, or fresh juices. For a splash of elegance, serve a big pitcher of sangria (light on the wine) or a bucket of cava.

If you are bringing beer, go for cans instead of bottles. Cans are lighter, easier to store, and less likely to break. For wine, choose rosé or white, and keep them chilled in a cooler. Red wine is a bad idea because it stains and warms up too fast. You can also bring cocktail ingredients if you want to mix drinks, but keep it simple: gin and tonic, mojito (pre-made), or a simple rum and coke.

One more thing: avoid sugary cocktails that can make seasickness worse. Stick to clear spirits and mixers. And if you are prone to sea sickness, skip the alcohol altogether and take ginger tablets instead. The skipper will thank you.

How to serve food on a moving boat

Presentation matters, but practicality matters more. Use non-slip trays or placemats to stop plates sliding. Serve food in shallow bowls or on plates with a lip to catch spills. Avoid tall glasses that tip over easily; use tumblers or stemless wine glasses. If you are anchoring in a calm bay like Cala del Faro, you can get away with a more elaborate setup. But if you are cruising, keep it simple.

Disposable plates and cutlery are fine for a casual party, but you can also rent melamine plates from some catering companies. They look nicer and are reusable. For a luxury charter, consider hiring a steward who will handle all the serving and cleaning. That way, you can relax and enjoy the views of La Concha mountain and the coastline.

Timing is also important. Serve food when the boat is stationary, either at anchor or docked. That reduces the risk of spills and makes eating more pleasant. Most charters include a stop for swimming, which is a perfect time to lay out the buffet.

Budgeting for your boat party catering

Your budget depends on the level of service you want. Here is a rough breakdown:

OptionCost per personWhat you get
DIY supermarketEUR 10-15Basic snacks, drinks, and salads
Takeaway from restaurantEUR 15-25Hot or cold dishes delivered to marina
Private catererEUR 40-80Full menu, setup, and sometimes service
Private chef on boardEUR 80-150Custom menu, cooking on the boat, premium experience

These are estimates and can vary based on the season and specific requests. For a group of six, the DIY option is fine. For a party of 12 or more, a caterer saves you hassle. And if you are celebrating something special, go for the private chef. You can find more ideas on our blog about planning the perfect day on the water.

Common questions

Can I bring my own food and drink on a charter boat in Marbella?

Yes, most charter companies allow you to bring your own catering. Check with the skipper first, as some may have restrictions on glass bottles or open flames. You are responsible for cleanup, so bring bin bags.

Do I need to tip the caterer or chef?

Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated. If the service is good, 10-15% of the catering cost is standard. For a private chef, you can tip EUR 20-50 depending on the quality.

What if someone gets seasick during the meal?

Have ginger biscuits or crackers on hand. Avoid greasy or spicy foods before the trip. If someone feels unwell, move them to the shaded area and let them sip water.

Are there vegetarian-friendly options for boat parties?

Absolutely. Spanish cuisine has many vegetarian dishes like gazpacho, tortilla española (egg and potato), and grilled vegetables. Most caterers can adapt menus on request.

How far in advance should I book catering?

For a private caterer or chef, book at least one week ahead, especially in peak season (June to September). For restaurant takeaway, 24-48 hours is usually enough.

Can I have a barbecue on a charter boat?

Some boats have a built-in barbecue, but many do not due to fire safety. If you want grilled food, ask the skipper if a portable barbecue is allowed. Alternatively, order grilled items from a caterer.

What drinks should I avoid on a boat party?

Red wine and dark spirits can stain and cause dehydration. Sugary cocktails can worsen seasickness. Stick to light drinks like cava, beer, or gin and tonic.

Seasonal catering: summer vs winter boat parties

Marbella's seasons dictate what works on a boat. In summer (June to September), temperatures hit 30-35 degrees C, so you want light, cold food that won't spoil in the heat. Think gazpacho shots, ceviche, and chilled seafood platters. Avoid anything with mayonnaise or dairy left out too long. In winter (November to March), the weather is cooler at 15-20 degrees C, and you can get away with heartier fare like hot soup in thermoses, empanadas, and chorizo al vino (chorizo cooked in wine). The shorter daylight hours mean you might eat at the dock before sunset, so consider a pre-ordered dinner from a nearby restaurant in Estepona old town.

The wind is another factor. In summer, the Levante wind can kick up choppy seas, especially around the Strait of Gibraltar. If you are heading out from Sotogrande or Cabopino, pack food that stays put in a container with a lid. In winter, the Poniente wind is calmer but cooler, so bring a thermos of hot chocolate or coffee to warm up after a swim (if you dare). Local caterers in Puerto Banús adjust their menus seasonally, so ask about summer salads or winter stews.

For a summer party, a stop at Cala del Faro for a swim and a cold buffet is ideal. For winter, consider a sunset cruise from Marbella Marina with a pre-arranged tapas box from a local deli. The key is to match the menu to the weather, not the other way around.

Catering for specific boat types: from RIBs to superyachts

The size and layout of your boat change what you can serve. On a RIB or speedboat, space is tight and there is no galley. Stick to pre-packaged snacks like nuts, crisps, and sandwiches in a cool bag. Drinks should be cans or plastic bottles. No glass, as it can break on the fibreglass. For a fishing boat, you have more deck space but still limited prep areas. A seafood platter with pre-peeled prawns and crab claws works well, served on a disposable tray.

On a catamaran, you have a stable platform and often a decent galley. This is where you can go all out with a paella cooked on board or a buffet of Spanish tortilla, grilled vegetables, and jamón. The wide deck allows for a proper table setup. For a sailing yacht, the galley is small but functional. Pre-prepared dishes that just need reheating are best. Think lasagne or chicken tagine in foil containers.

For a superyacht, you can hire a private chef who uses the full kitchen. Expect multi-course meals with wine pairings, from lobster thermidor to chocolate fondant. The cost is higher, but the experience is unmatched. If you are chartering from Benalmádena, some superyachts have a barbecue on the flybridge, perfect for grilled fish and chorizo skewers. Check with BoatHire24 for specific boat amenities before ordering.

Pairing food with departure ports and routes

Each port on the Costa del Sol has local specialities that work for a boat party. From Puerto Banús, order from the high-end tapas bars like La Sala or Bibo. Their takeaway menus include mini burgers, tuna tartare, and truffle croquettes. From Marbella Marina, try the chiringuitos (beach bars) for grilled sardines and espetos (skewered fish). These are messy but delicious, and the locals know how to pack them for boats.

If you depart from Cabopino, the port has a quieter vibe with a few seafood restaurants. Order a mixed seafood platter with prawns, clams, and octopus. From Estepona, the old town has bakeries selling empanadas and pastries. A stop at the market for fresh fruit and cheese is easy. From Sotogrande, the marina has upscale delis with gourmet sandwiches and salads. For a trip towards the Strait of Gibraltar, pack light food because the currents can be strong. Dolphin watching tours often include a simple lunch of baguettes and fruit.

For a longer route to Nerja caves, plan a full meal. The journey takes 2-3 hours each way, so you need substantial food. A paella or fideuà (noodle paella) from a restaurant in Marbella, packed in foil, works well. Serve it at anchor near the caves before heading back.
