title: New Years Eve Yacht Party Marbella
excerpt: Ring in the new year on the water with a New Years Eve yacht party in Marbella. From Puerto Banús fireworks to champagne on deck, here's how to book your floating fiesta.
metaDescription: Book a New Years Eve yacht party in Marbella with BoatHire24. Enjoy Puerto Banús fireworks, champagne, and a skipper. Start 2025 from EUR 1,200.
author: Mardo Soo
content:
The 30-second answer

If you want to spend New Year's Eve somewhere other than a crowded club or a stuffy hotel restaurant, a New Years Eve yacht party in Marbella is your move. You get a private boat, a licensed skipper, a front-row seat to the Puerto Banús fireworks, and all the cava you can drink. Prices start from around EUR 1,200 for a small motor yacht for up to 8 guests, and you can book through BoatHire24 with no hidden fees. Departures run from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande, and Benalmádena. Just don't expect to be sober when the clock strikes twelve.

Why a yacht beats a nightclub on NYE

Marbella's nightclubs on New Year's Eve are a circus. You queue for an hour, pay EUR 200 for a ticket that includes one warm drink, and then stand shoulder-to-shoulder with strangers while someone spills beer on your shoes. On a yacht, you control the guest list, the music, and the temperature. You can anchor near the Puerto Banús harbour mouth and watch the midnight fireworks without elbowing anyone. The sea air keeps you cool, and you have a private toilet onboard, which is more than you can say for most clubs. Plus, you get a licensed skipper who handles the navigation, so you can focus on drinking champagne and looking at the stars. For groups of 6 to 12, a yacht party often works out cheaper per person than a VIP table at a club, especially when you factor in the free-flowing booze you bring yourself. And if the weather turns, you can retreat to the heated cabin below. No refunds for rain, but at least you stay dry.

Which boat type works for NYE parties

Not all boats are built for partying. A sailing yacht with a low cockpit and a furled mainsail might look romantic, but it offers limited space for dancing. For a New Years Eve yacht party in Marbella, you want a motor yacht or a catamaran. Motor yachts from around 40 feet have a spacious aft deck where you can set up a speaker and a small table for drinks. The flybridge gives you an elevated view of the fireworks, and the cabin below provides a warm refuge if the wind picks up. Catamarans are even better because they don't heel, so your champagne glasses stay upright. They also have a trampoline net at the bow where guests can sit and dangle their feet over the water. RIBs and speedboats are too small for a party unless you only have four people. Licence-free day boats are fine for a quiet cruise but lack the power and amenities for a proper celebration. Superyachts are available for those with a budget of EUR 10,000 or more, and they come with a crew who will serve you canapés and mix cocktails. For most groups, a 40- to 50-foot motor yacht or a 38- to 45-foot catamaran is the sweet spot. Check the search page to filter by size and price.

Departure ports and fireworks views

The best view of the New Year's Eve fireworks in Marbella is from the water, but your exact vantage point depends on where you depart from. Puerto Banús is the main event. The harbour launches a 10-minute pyrotechnic display at midnight, and you can anchor just outside the breakwater for a perfect sightline. Boats leaving from Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) have a longer cruise to reach the action, about 20 minutes at 8 knots, but you can also watch the smaller fireworks from the Marbella promenade. Cabopino is quieter, with a small local display, so you get intimacy but less spectacle. Estepona old town has a charming square celebration with fireworks over the sea, and Sotogrande offers a more upscale, low-key vibe. Benalmádena is the wildcard: its marina has a big party with live music, and you can anchor near the Puerto Marina bridge for the show. If you want to see the Gibraltar Strait dolphins on the way back, book a late departure from Estepona or Sotogrande. Just remember that the skipper will not rush the return trip, so factor in an extra hour for the cruise back to port. Most charters run from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m., but you can negotiate a longer hire for an additional fee.

What to bring and what to expect from the skipper

You are responsible for your own food and drink on a bareboat-style charter, even with a skipper. The boat will have a fridge and often an ice box, so bring champagne, beer, mixers, and snacks. Do not bring glass bottles if you can avoid it; plastic or cans are safer on deck. The skipper will provide safety briefings and keep the boat stable, but they will not serve drinks or clean up after you. You can hire a catering package through BoatHire24 for around EUR 30 per person, which includes tapas and a bottle of cava per guest. For the midnight toast, bring a good bottle of something sparkly, because the cheap stuff tastes worse when it is warm. Dress in layers. Marbella in December averages 15 degrees C during the day and drops to 10 degrees C at night. On the water, the wind chill makes it feel colder. A smart jacket or a pashmina works, and deck shoes with non-slip soles are non-negotiable. The skipper will have a VHF radio and will monitor the weather, so if a storm rolls in, they will cancel the trip and refund your deposit. But the Costa del Sol rarely gets serious winter storms, so you are probably safe.

Cost breakdown and booking tips

A New Years Eve yacht party in Marbella costs between EUR 1,200 and EUR 3,500 for a standard motor yacht or catamaran for up to 12 guests. This includes the skipper, fuel for the local cruising area, and basic insurance. You will pay extra for catering, a longer cruising range, or a superyacht. Deposit is typically 50% at booking, with the balance due 14 days before departure. Cancel up to 30 days out for a full refund, but after that, you lose the deposit. Book early. December 31 is the busiest night of the year, and boats get snapped up by November. If you wait until December 20, you will only find leftover options at inflated prices. Use the search filter to set your budget and guest count, then message the owner directly through the platform. Do not pay by bank transfer to a random account; use the secure payment system on BoatHire24. One more tip: if you want to avoid the crowds, book a daytime cruise on December 30 or January 1 instead. The weather is the same, the price is lower, and you get the sea to yourself.

Local colour: what to do before and after the party

Before you step aboard, spend the afternoon in Puerto Banús. Walk along the marina and look at the superyachts, then grab a coffee at one of the harbour-front cafés. If you want a proper meal, book a table at a restaurant on the Muelle de Honor, but do it weeks in advance. For a more relaxed vibe, head to the Río Verde area and have lunch at a chiringuito on the beach. After the yacht party ends around 2 a.m., you can walk from the marina to any of the clubs on the Golden Mile, like Pangea or Olivia's, but expect a queue. Alternatively, call a taxi and go to Estepona old town, where the street party continues until dawn with live flamenco and churros stalls. If you are staying in Marbella centre, the Avenida del Mar has a free outdoor concert and a giant clock for the countdown. The next day, sleep in and then cure your hangover with a walk up La Concha mountain. The trail starts from the Istan road and takes about two hours to the summit. Or take a gentle stroll along the Marbella promenade from the marina to the Faro de Marbella lighthouse, a 3 km flat walk with sea views. If you have more energy, drive to the Nerja caves, about an hour east, and marvel at the stalactites. Just do not drive if you are still over the limit. Taxis are cheap and plentiful.

Weather and sea conditions on NYE

December in Marbella is mild but unpredictable. Average daytime temperature is 16 degrees C, and sea temperature is around 15 degrees C, so you will not want to swim. Wind speeds typically range from 5 to 15 knots, which is fine for a motor yacht but can make a catamaran rock slightly. The skipper will monitor the forecast and may adjust the anchorage to avoid the worst of the swell. If the wind exceeds 25 knots or there is a storm warning, the charter will be cancelled for safety, and you get a full refund. Rain is rare, with only 6 days of precipitation in December on average, but it can happen. Bring a waterproof jacket just in case. The sun sets around 6:15 p.m. in late December, so your departure at 10 p.m. means you will cruise in the dark. The boat's navigation lights and cabin lights create a cosy atmosphere, and the stars are bright away from the city lights. Do not expect a calm, glassy sea. The Mediterranean in winter has a slight chop, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar, but it is not rough enough to cause seasickness for most people. If you are prone to motion sickness, take a tablet an hour before departure and stick to the lower deck.

Common questions

Can we bring our own alcohol on a New Years Eve yacht party in Marbella?

Yes, you can bring your own alcohol. Most charters allow you to bring whatever you want, but check the terms when you book. Some owners prohibit red wine because it stains the upholstery, so stick to white wine, champagne, beer, and spirits. Bring plastic cups to avoid broken glass on deck.

Is there a minimum age for guests on the yacht?

There is no minimum age for guests, but the skipper has the final say on safety. Children are welcome on most boats, but you need to inform the owner in advance. For parties with alcohol, the skipper may ask for ID if guests look under 18. The legal drinking age in Spain is 18.

What happens if the weather is bad on December 31?

If the skipper decides the weather is unsafe, the charter will be cancelled and you get a full refund. This is rare, but it happens maybe once every five years. If the weather is marginal, the skipper may offer a shorter cruise or a different anchorage. You cannot demand a refund for light rain or moderate wind.

How many people can fit on a typical NYE yacht?

Motor yachts and catamarans for charter usually accommodate between 6 and 12 guests. The maximum is set by the boat's safety certificate, which is based on life raft capacity and deck space. Do not try to sneak extra guests onboard; the skipper will count heads before departure.

Do we need to tip the skipper?

Tipping is not mandatory but is appreciated. A standard tip is 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee, handed in cash at the end of the trip. If the skipper goes above and beyond, like helping with decorations or providing a Bluetooth speaker, tip more. If the service is poor, you are not obligated to tip.

Can we play our own music on the boat?

Yes, most boats have a Bluetooth stereo or an auxiliary input. Bring your own playlist or use a streaming service. Keep the volume reasonable, especially after midnight when other boats are anchored nearby. The skipper may ask you to lower it if neighbours complain.

Is there a toilet onboard?

Yes, all boats available for charter have a marine toilet (head) in a small cabin. It flushes with seawater, so do not put anything other than toilet paper and human waste down it. The skipper will give you a briefing on how to use it. If you clog it, you may be charged a cleaning fee.

title: Boat Photoshoot Marbella Poses
excerpt: Capture the perfect boat photoshoot in Marbella with these poses, tips, and location ideas for Puerto Banús, Estepona, and the Costa del Sol.
metaDescription: Boat photoshoot Marbella poses: expert tips for stunning shots on yachts, catamarans, and RIBs. Best spots in Puerto Banús, Estepona, and more.
author: Mardo Soo
content:
The 30-second answer

For a boat photoshoot in Marbella, you want poses that work with the Mediterranean light, the boat's lines, and the backdrop of Puerto Banús or the Costa del Sol. Think leaning on the rail, sitting on the bow with legs dangling, or a candid shot at the helm. Keep it natural, use the golden hour, and avoid stiff smiles. You'll find that simple adjustments, like turning your body towards the sun or holding a glass of cava, make the difference between a holiday snap and a magazine cover.

Why Marbella is a boat photoshoot paradise

Marbella and the Costa del Sol offer a unique mix for boat photoshoots. You have the glitz of BoatHire24 yachts in Puerto Banús, the wild coastline near Cabopino, and the historic charm of Estepona's old town visible from the water. The light here is intense, especially from 11am to 3pm, so you need to work with shadows. But the real magic happens at sunrise and sunset, when La Concha mountain turns pink and the sea becomes glass. You can charter anything from a sleek motor yacht to a sailing boat, each giving a different vibe. A catamaran offers a wide deck for group shots, while a RIB gives that sporty, wind-in-your-hair look. The key is to match the boat to the mood you want: luxury, adventure, or romance.

Top poses for a boat photoshoot in Marbella

Let's get into the specifics. These poses work on most boats, from the 10-metre motor yachts to the 20-metre catamarans. You should adjust based on the deck space and safety rails.

  • Bow sit with legs dangling. Sit on the forward deck, legs over the side, facing the camera or looking out to sea. This works best when the boat is anchored, not moving fast. The bow of a sailing yacht or motor yacht gives a classic frame.
  • Helm shot. Stand behind the wheel, one hand on it, looking ahead or back with a smirk. The skipper can be blurred in the background. This screams 'I'm in charge', even if you're not.
  • Rail lean. Lean sideways on the railing, arms crossed or one hand holding a drink. Turn your face towards the sun to avoid shadows on your eyes. This is the go-to for Instagram.
  • Sun lounger chill. Lie back on a sun pad, sunglasses on, book or phone in hand. It's relaxed and shows the luxury side of the charter.
  • Walking the deck. Walk towards the camera, looking down or laughing. This candid style works well on catamarans where you have more space.
  • Group toast. Everyone holds a glass of something bubbly, clink, and laugh. The boat's table or flybridge is the spot. Keep the drinks low to avoid blocking faces.

Best times of day for your photoshoot

You have two windows for the best light: sunrise (around 7am in summer, 8am in winter) and the golden hour before sunset (5pm to 7pm, depending on the season). Midday light is harsh and creates deep shadows under your eyes and the boat's bimini. If you must shoot at midday, use a reflector or shoot in the shade of the boat's cabin. The water colour changes too: early morning it's a deep blue, midday it's turquoise, and sunset it turns gold. For a luxury vibe, aim for the hour before sunset when Puerto Banús lights start to reflect on the water. For a natural, bohemian look, sunrise with the sea calm is unbeatable.

Location ideas: where to anchor for the best backdrop

Your choice of anchorage affects the background of every shot. Here are four spots that work well for photoshoots on the Costa del Sol.

LocationVibeBest for
Puerto BanúsLuxury, glamYachts, superyachts, evening shots with lights
Cala del Faro (Cabopino)Wild, naturalCatamarans, sailing boats, beach shots
Estepona coastRomantic, old town backdropSunset, couple photos, RIBs
Strait of GibraltarAdventurous, dolphinsAction shots, wildlife, wide-angle

Each location gives a different feel. Puerto Banús is perfect for the 'rich and famous' look, with the marina's superyachts and designer shops in the background. Cala del Faro offers a more secluded, natural setting with cliffs and pine trees. Estepona's coast has the old town's white buildings behind you, and the Strait of Gibraltar is where you might spot dolphins, adding a wild element to your shoot.

What to wear for a boat photoshoot

Keep it simple and avoid busy patterns. White, cream, navy, and pastel colours work best because they contrast with the blue sea and white boat. For women, a flowing dress or a jumpsuit is ideal; for men, linen trousers and a white shirt or polo. Swimwear is fine if you're going for a beach vibe, but cover-ups like a kaftan or a light jacket add sophistication. Avoid heels on the boat (dangerous and impractical) and go for flat sandals or espadrilles. Sunglasses are a must, but take them off for some shots to show your eyes. Hats can work, but they cast shadows on your face, so tilt them back or use them only in profile shots.

Camera settings and gear tips

You don't need a professional camera, but if you have one, use a wide-angle lens (24-70mm) for full-body shots and a telephoto (70-200mm) for candid portraits. For smartphones, use portrait mode and tap on the subject's face to lock exposure. Avoid digital zoom, which kills quality. Shoot in raw if possible, or at least in HDR mode on a phone. A polarising filter reduces glare on the water and makes the sky pop. For video, use a gimbal to stabilise the wobble of the boat. And always bring a waterproof bag for your gear, because salt spray is not your friend.

Hiring a boat for your photoshoot

You can book a boat for a photoshoot through BoatHire24's search page, filtering by size and type. Most charters include a skipper, so you can focus on the shoot while they handle the boat. Prices vary, but expect from around EUR 300 for a half-day on a smaller motor yacht, up to EUR 1,500 for a large catamaran or superyacht. You should confirm with the skipper that you can anchor for photos, and ask about the boat's policy on props like champagne or inflatables. Some boats have strict rules on glassware, so use plastic flutes. The skipper can also suggest the best spots based on wind and sea conditions, which is invaluable.

Common mistakes to avoid

First, don't plan too many poses in a tight space. A 10-metre boat gets crowded fast. Pick three or four poses and do them well. Second, ignore the sun position at your peril. You'll end up with squinting subjects or harsh shadows. Third, forget to check the boat's condition before the shoot. A dirty deck or faded cushions ruin the luxury feel. Fourth, skip the backup plan. If the sea is rough, you can't shoot on the bow, so have interior or helm shots ready. Finally, don't rush. A boat photoshoot should feel relaxed, not like a military operation. Take breaks, enjoy the sea, and the best shots will come naturally.

Common questions

What is the best boat for a photoshoot in Marbella? It depends on the look you want. A motor yacht offers sleek lines and a luxury feel. A catamaran gives more deck space for group shots. A sailing yacht has a classic, romantic vibe. RIBs are good for action shots but limited for poses.

Do I need a permit for a boat photoshoot in Marbella? No, but if you're shooting for commercial use (advertising, stock photography), you may need a permit from the port authority. For personal or social media use, no permit is needed, but check with your charter company.

Can I bring a professional photographer on the boat? Yes, most charters allow extra guests. You should inform the skipper in advance, especially if you're bringing heavy equipment. Some boats charge a small surcharge for additional passengers.

How long does a boat photoshoot take? Typically 2-3 hours, including travel time to the anchorage. Half-day charters (4 hours) give you enough time for two locations and multiple outfit changes. Full-day charters (8 hours) allow for a lunch break and sunset shots.

What if the weather is bad? Most charters offer a free reschedule if the forecast is poor. If you're already on the water, the skipper can adjust the route to find calmer areas, like the lee side of a headland. Always have a backup date.

Can I bring props like balloons or inflatables? Yes, but check with the skipper first. Some boats ban inflatables due to safety concerns. If you're using champagne or wine, use plastic glasses to avoid breakage. And take all props with you when you leave.

Are there any restrictions on drone photography? Yes, drones are banned in many areas of the Costa del Sol, including near airports and crowded beaches. You need a permit from AESA (Spanish aviation authority) for commercial drone use. For personal use, keep the drone away from other boats and people.

Posing on different boat types: motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs

Each boat type demands a different approach to posing. On a motor yacht, you have clean lines and a flybridge that works for elevated shots. Stand at the top of the stairs to the flybridge, one hand on the rail, looking down at the camera for a power pose. The aft deck, with its U-shaped seating, is ideal for group shots where everyone leans in. On a catamaran, the trampoline net at the bow is a unique spot: lie on your stomach, chin on hands, legs up, or sit cross-legged for a bohemian look. The wide beam means you can shoot two people walking side by side. For a RIB or speedboat, the vibe is sporty. Sit on the tube edge, legs over the side, holding the grab handle. Or stand at the console, sunglasses on, looking back at the wake. Avoid complex poses on a RIB because the boat bounces more.

Seasonal considerations for your Marbella boat photoshoot

Summer (June to September) offers long days, sea temperatures around 24-26 degrees C, and calm mornings. But it also brings crowds, especially in Puerto Banús, and a harsh midday sun. Book a 7am to 10am slot to avoid the chaos. Spring (April to May) and autumn (October) are the sweet spots: fewer boats, softer light, and air temperatures of 20-25 degrees C. The water is cooler, around 18 degrees C, so swimsuit shots are brief. Winter (November to March) is risky for sea conditions, but you can get dramatic shots with grey skies and big waves, perfect for a moody, editorial look. The sun is lower all day, so you have a longer golden hour. Just bring a jacket because it can drop to 12 degrees C on the water.

Using the Marbella coastline as your backdrop

Beyond the obvious spots, consider the Río Verde estuary, where the river meets the sea near Puerto Banús. The sandbanks and dunes give a wild, natural contrast to the yacht. For a shot with La Concha mountain behind you, anchor off Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) and face east in the afternoon. The mountain's jagged peak frames the boat. If you want a more urban backdrop, the Benalmádena coast has the marina's pagoda-style buildings and the cable car station on the hill. For a truly unique shot, head towards the Nerja cliffs (a longer trip, about 30 NM from Marbella), where the whitewashed balconies of Europe hang over the sea. The journey itself can be a photoshoot, with the coastline unfolding behind you.

Posing with props and accessories

Props add interest without making the shot look staged. A straw hat works well if you hold it by the brim rather than wearing it, so it doesn't cast a shadow. A white towel draped over your shoulders suggests a day of relaxation. For a luxury feel, use a bottle of cava (label facing the camera) and two flutes, but remember to use plastic glasses to avoid breakage. Inflatables like a flamingo or unicorn are popular for catamaran shoots, but they need calm water and a dedicated crew member to keep them in frame. Avoid anything that screams 'brand' unless you're paid for it. The best prop is the boat itself: the steering wheel, the winches on a sailing boat, or the anchor chain make for natural, tactile shots.

Working with the skipper and crew during the shoot

The skipper is your best ally. They know the local wind patterns, the quiet coves, and the legalities of anchoring. Brief them before the shoot: tell them the vibe you want, the poses you plan, and whether you need the boat stationary or moving. For bow shots, the boat must be anchored or at low speed (under 5 knots) for safety. The crew can help by adjusting the boat's position so the sun hits the subject's face, or by spraying a fine mist of water for a 'sea spray' effect. They can also hold reflectors or move props. Tip them EUR 20-50 for their help, especially if they go beyond the standard charter duties.

Editing and posting your boat photos

After the shoot, editing is where the magic happens. Use presets that boost blues and whites while keeping skin tones natural. Avoid over-saturation, which makes the sea look fake. Crop to remove the horizon line if it's not level, and use the healing brush to erase any litter or other boats in the background. For Instagram, vertical 4:5 crops work best for feed posts, while 9:16 is for Reels and Stories. Post within 48 hours of the shoot to capitalise on the excitement. Tag the charter company and the location (e.g., Puerto Banús, Marbella) to increase reach. Use hashtags like #MarbellaBoatPhotoshoot, #CostaDelSolYacht, and #PuertoBanúsLuxury, but keep it to 5-10 relevant ones.

Cost breakdown for a boat photoshoot in Marbella

Here is a rough guide to what you might spend. A half-day charter (4 hours) on a 10-metre motor yacht costs from around EUR 300 to EUR 500. A catamaran of similar size is EUR 400 to EUR 700. A professional photographer in Marbella charges EUR 150 to EUR 400 per hour, depending on experience and equipment. Hair and makeup artists start at EUR 100 for the session. Props and styling (outfits, accessories) can add EUR 50 to EUR 200. Total for a half-day shoot with a photographer and stylist: EUR 800 to EUR 1,500. For a full-day shoot with multiple locations and outfit changes, budget EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000. Always confirm what is included: fuel, skipper, cleaning fees, and VAT.

title: Marbella Boat Party for Stag Do
excerpt: A Marbella boat party for a stag do means sun, sea, and a private yacht with a skipper. No queues, no crowds, just your group and the Costa del Sol coastline.
metaDescription: Plan a Marbella boat party for a stag do: private yacht, skipper, and open bar. Depart from Puerto Banús or Marbella. Book your stag boat hire now.
author: Mardo Soo
content:
The 30-second answer

If you are organising a stag do in Marbella and want something that does not involve queuing for a crowded club, a Marbella boat party for stag do is the answer. You hire a private motor yacht or catamaran from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day, the skipper handles everything, and you get a floating VIP area with sun decks, a sound system, and an open bar. Depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or Estepona, cruise past La Concha mountain, drop anchor for a swim, and return in time for dinner. No hangover from planning, just a hangover from the party.

Why a boat party works for a stag do

A stag do on a boat avoids the usual chaos of trying to get a big group into a restaurant or club on time. You have your own space, your own music, and your own drinks. No one gets lost. No one argues about the bill. The skipper keeps the boat steady, the sun keeps the mood up, and the Mediterranean keeps the temperature around 28 degrees C in summer. You can swim, sunbathe, and take photos of the coast without a thousand strangers in the frame.

Marbella has more than 300 days of sunshine a year, so the weather is rarely an issue. The water is calm in the bay, especially between Puerto Banús and Cabopino, which means even the queasy types can handle it. You can bring your own playlist, or the boat crew will put on something that suits. Most charters include a cooler with ice, so you bring the beer and the groom’s favourite spirit.

The key advantage is privacy. You are not sharing the boat with other groups. It is just your lads, the skipper, and maybe a hostess if you book a premium package. That means you can do whatever you want within reason, jump off the bow, blast music, or just lie on the deck and recover from the night before. For more details on boat types and pricing, check the Marbella boat hire search.

Best departure ports for a stag boat party

You have several options for where to start your Marbella boat party for stag do. Each port has its own vibe, and the choice affects the route and the views.

  • Puerto Banús: The most famous marina on the Costa del Sol. You walk past superyachts and flashy cars to get to your boat. The route goes past the golden sands of San Pedro and the Cala del Faro cliffs. Good for a group that wants to feel like a millionaire for a day.
  • Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo): Central, near the old town, and slightly less flashy than Banús. You cruise east towards Cabopino, passing the dunes and the nudist beach. Cheaper mooring fees mean the boat hire rates can be a bit lower.
  • Estepona: Quieter and more laid-back. The old town is a 10-minute walk from the marina, so you can start with a few beers at a terrace bar. The route goes towards the Strait of Gibraltar, where you often see dolphins. Good for a stag do that wants a bit of wildlife with their booze.
  • Sotogrande: Exclusive and spread out. The marina is surrounded by golf courses and luxury villas. The water is very calm because it is inside the Guadiaro river mouth. Best for a group that wants to avoid the crowds entirely.
  • Benalmádena: A bit further east, near Torremolinos. The marina has a lively nightlife, and the boat route passes the Castillo de Colomares. Good if your group is staying on that side of Malaga.

Most charters include pickup from the port of your choice, but you need to get the group there. Taxis or minibuses work. If the groom is feeling generous, a private transfer can be arranged through the charter company.

Boat types for a stag party

Not all boats are equal a stag do. You need space, shade, and a decent sound system. Here are the main options.

Boat typeCapacityTypical price half-dayBest for
Motor yacht10-20 guestsFrom EUR 1,800Speed, style, and a sundeck
Catamaran12-30 guestsFrom EUR 2,200Stability and lots of deck space
Sailing yacht8-14 guestsFrom EUR 1,200A quieter, more relaxed vibe
RIB / speedboat6-10 guestsFrom EUR 800Adrenaline and small groups
Superyacht20+ guestsPrice on requestUltimate luxury and bragging rights

For a standard stag do of 10 to 15 guys, a motor yacht or catamaran is the sweet spot. Motor yachts are faster, so you can cover more coastline. Catamarans are more stable, which helps if anyone is nursing a hangover. Both come with a licensed skipper who knows the best anchor spots. You can also add a hostess or a DJ for an extra fee. Browse the full selection on BoatHire24 to compare options.

What to include in your stag boat package

A basic Marbella boat party for stag do includes the boat, the skipper, and fuel for a standard route. But you can upgrade with extras that make the day feel special.

  • Open bar: Most charters offer a drinks package with beer, wine, soft drinks, and water. Spirits cost extra. Typical price: EUR 25-40 per person for a half-day.
  • Food: A barbecue on the boat works well. Paella, burgers, or a seafood spread. Or you can bring your own tapas from a local supermarket. Catering starts from EUR 20 per person.
  • Water toys: A paddleboard, a doughnut inflatable towed behind the boat, or snorkeling gear. Adds fun for the lads who want to cool off.
  • Music system: Bluetooth speakers are standard, but you can request a proper DJ setup with a subwoofer. Some boats have a built-in sound system with a mixer.
  • Hostess or steward: Someone to serve drinks, handle the food, and make sure the groom does not fall overboard. Price on request.
  • Photographer: A professional to capture the group shots and the groom’s inevitable face-plant into the sea. From EUR 150 extra.

Do not forget the essentials: sun cream, sunglasses, a hat, and a spare T-shirt. The Mediterranean sun is no joke, and a sunburnt groom is not a happy groom.

Sample itinerary for a half-day stag party

Here is a typical schedule if you depart from Puerto Banús at 11:00. Adjust the times based on your charter.

  • 11:00: Board at Puerto Banús. Meet the skipper, sign the paperwork, and get the safety briefing. Start the drinks.
  • 11:30: Depart. Cruise east along the coast. Pass the Marbella skyline and the La Concha mountain. The skipper points out the mansions of the rich and famous.
  • 12:15: Drop anchor near Cabopino. The water is calm and clear. Jump in, swim, use the paddleboard. The crew fires up the barbecue if you ordered one.
  • 13:00: Lunch and more drinks. Music plays. Group photos with the coast in the background.
  • 14:00: Weigh anchor and cruise back towards Puerto Banús. Pass the Cala del Faro cliffs. The skipper might let someone steer for a photo.
  • 14:45: Dock at Puerto Banús. Disembark. Head to a beach club or a tapas bar for the afternoon.

If you want a full-day trip, you can go as far as Estepona or even the Strait of Gibraltar to see dolphins. That adds 2-3 hours of cruising each way, so budget for extra fuel costs.

Legal stuff and safety for a stag group

Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who holds a Spanish professional qualification. They are responsible for the boat and the safety of everyone on board. You do not need a licence yourself, but you must follow the skipper’s instructions.

Alcohol is allowed, but the skipper has the right to refuse service if someone is dangerously drunk. They will not let you drive the boat. If anyone falls overboard, the skipper will stop and retrieve them. Life jackets are provided and must be worn if the skipper says so, usually in rough conditions or at night.

Most boats have a maximum capacity that includes the crew. Do not try to sneak extra guests on board. The skipper checks the manifest before departure. Overloading is illegal and unsafe. If you want to bring your own drinks, check with the charter company first. Some boats have a corkage fee.

For more tips on planning a stag do on the water, read our blog about boat party etiquette and packing lists.

Cost breakdown for a Marbella stag boat party

The total cost depends on the boat size, duration, extras, and the number of guests. Here is a rough guide for a group of 12 people on a half-day motor yacht departing from Puerto Banús.

Prices vary by season. July and August are peak, so expect a 20-30% premium. May, June, and September offer better value and still great weather. You can save by bringing your own drinks and food, but check the boat’s policy first.

Common questions

How many people can I bring on a Marbella boat party for stag do?
Most boats accommodate 10 to 20 guests. Catamarans can hold up to 30. Check the specific boat’s capacity on the listing.

Do I need a licence to hire a boat for a stag party?
No. Every charter includes a licensed skipper who handles the navigation. You just relax and party.

Can we play our own music?
Yes. Most boats have Bluetooth speakers or an auxiliary input. Some have a DJ setup for an extra fee.

What happens if the weather is bad?
The skipper decides if it is safe to sail. If they cancel due to weather, you get a full refund or a reschedule. If you cancel on the day, you may lose the deposit.

Can we swim from the boat?
Yes, when the skipper drops anchor in a safe spot. Life jackets are available for non-swimmers.

Is there a toilet on board?
Most motor yachts and catamarans have a marine toilet. Smaller RIBs may not. Check the boat details before booking.

How far in advance should I book?
At least two weeks in summer. One week in shoulder months. Last-minute bookings are possible but limit your choice of boats.

How to choose the right package size for your stag group

The number of lads in your group determines the boat type and the budget per head. For a group of 6 to 10, a RIB or a small motor yacht works well. You get speed and a more intimate vibe, and the cost per person stays under EUR 200 for a half-day with drinks. For 10 to 15, a motor yacht between 12 and 15 metres is the standard choice. You have enough deck space for everyone to spread out, and the skipper can anchor in a quiet cove near Cabopino without overcrowding.

For 15 to 25 guests, a catamaran is the smart move. Catamarans have a wider beam, so the deck feels like a floating terrace. You can fit a barbecue, a cooler full of beer, and still have room for a dance-off. The stability also means fewer seasick moments, which matters if the groom had one too many the night before. For groups over 25, you start looking at superyachts or two boats running together. That gets expensive, but the bragging rights are real. Always confirm the maximum capacity with the charter company before you book, because the legal limit includes the crew. If you try to squeeze an extra mate on board, the skipper will say no.

If your group is split between party animals and those who want a quieter day, consider a catamaran with a flybridge. The party crowd can stay on the main deck with the music, while the tired ones nap on the flybridge cushions. That flexibility is hard to beat. Check the Marbella boat hire search for boats with flybridge options.

The best time of year for a stag boat party in Marbella

Summer is the obvious choice, but it comes with trade-offs. July and August bring 32 degrees C, packed marinas, and premium prices. The water is warm at 24-26 degrees C, so swimming is effortless. But Puerto Banús is heaving with tourists, and finding a berth for your boat can take extra time. If you book in August, do it at least three weeks ahead and expect to pay 20-30% more than June rates.

May and June are the sweet spot for a stag do. The temperature sits around 25-28 degrees C, the sea is calm, and the crowds are thinner. Prices are lower, and you have more choice of boats. The only downside is the water is cooler, around 18-20 degrees C in May, but still swimmable if you are brave. September is similar, with the added bonus of the summer holiday rush ending, so marinas are quieter and the sunset cruises are spectacular.

Winter months from November to March are not ideal for a boat party. The temperature drops to 15-18 degrees C, and the sea can be choppy. Some charters still run, but you will spend most of the time inside the cabin. If you are set on a winter stag, pick a motor yacht with a heated saloon and skip the swimming. The views of La Concha mountain with snow on top are a rare sight, but not worth freezing for.

How to handle the groom and the stag traditions on a boat

A boat party gives you a controlled environment for the classic stag rituals. The groom can be tied to the mast, if the boat has one, or you can rig a challenge like a plank walk off the bow. Just make sure the skipper is okay with it first. Some skippers allow light-hearted antics, others draw the line at anything that could damage the boat or cause injury. The key is to ask during the booking process, not on the day.

For the ceremonial first drink, start with a toast as you leave the marina. Use the champagne or cava from the open bar, and get a photo of the groom with the Marbella coast behind him. If you want a more memorable moment, arrange for the skipper to stop near the Cala del Faro cliffs, where the water is deep and clear. The groom can jump off the flybridge or the bow for a photo op. Just check the boat's height first, a 3-metre jump is fine, but 6 metres can hurt.

If your group wants to keep the party going after the boat, plan a transition. Many charter companies offer a package that includes a table at a nearby beach club or a VIP entry to a Puerto Banús club. That saves you the hassle of negotiating with bouncers while half your group is still drying off. For more ideas on combining boat hire with nightlife, read our blog on stag do itineraries in Marbella.

Hidden costs and how to avoid them

The advertised price for a boat hire often excludes a few items that can catch you out. Fuel is usually included for a standard route within the bay, but if you want to go to Estepona or the Strait of Gibraltar, expect a fuel surcharge of EUR 100-300 depending on the distance. Check the route limits before you book. Some charters also charge a cleaning fee of EUR 50-100 if the boat is left messy, so assign someone to collect empty bottles and cups before you dock.

Another common extra is the docking fee at the end of the trip. If you return to a different port than you departed from, the skipper may charge for the additional mooring. Stick to the same port unless you have a reason to change. Also, check if the boat has a marine toilet and if it requires a pump-out fee. Some smaller boats charge EUR 20-30 for using the toilet, which is annoying but avoidable if you use the facilities at the marina before boarding.

If you bring your own drinks, some charters add a corkage fee of EUR 5-10 per bottle of spirits. Beer and wine are usually fine without a fee, but confirm in advance. The best way to avoid surprises is to request a full price breakdown from the charter company before you pay the deposit. A reputable company will itemise everything, including VAT at 21%, which is sometimes not shown in the initial quote.

title: Marbella Boat Party for Stag Do Cost
excerpt: Marbella boat party for stag do cost breakdown: from roughly EUR 1,200 for a half-day RIB to EUR 6,000+ for a luxury motor yacht. Includes skipper, fuel and extras.
metaDescription: Marbella boat party for stag do cost: from EUR 1,200 for a RIB to EUR 6,000+ for a luxury yacht. Compare prices, inclusions and tips for your stag party.
author: Mardo Soo
content:
The 30-second answer

If you are organising a stag do in Marbella and thinking about a boat party, expect to pay from around EUR 1,200 for a half-day RIB or speedboat for up to 10 people, up to EUR 6,000 or more for a full-day luxury motor yacht with a crew. Most charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, and basic safety gear. You will also need to budget for food, drinks and any extras like a DJ or watersports. The final cost depends on the boat type, duration, number of guests and the season. For a typical stag group of 10-12, a decent half-day catamaran or motor yacht will set you back EUR 2,000-3,500. Always check what is included and book early, especially in July and August.

What determines the cost of a Marbella boat party for a stag do?

Several factors push the price up or down. The biggest is the boat type. A basic RIB or speedboat (6-8 metres) is the cheapest option, starting around EUR 1,200 for three hours. A sailing yacht or catamaran (12-15 metres) costs more, typically EUR 2,500-4,000 for a half day. A luxury motor yacht (over 20 metres) can hit EUR 6,000-10,000 for a full day. Then there is the duration: half-day (4 hours) versus full-day (8 hours). Most stag parties go for half-day, which is enough for a swim stop, drinks and some music. Full-day charters add lunch, a longer cruise and more time for watersports.

Number of guests matters too. Many boats have a maximum capacity of 10-12 passengers. If you have a bigger group, you might need two boats or a larger vessel, which increases the cost. Season is another factor. July and August are peak months, with prices 20-30% higher than May or September. Weekends are also more expensive than weekdays. Finally, extras add up: a DJ, a photographer, a barbecue, premium drinks, or watersports like jet skis or paddleboards. Some companies include a basic drinks package, but often you pay extra. Fuel is usually included, but check, some budget operators charge extra for longer cruises.

Typical price ranges by boat type

Here is a rough breakdown of what you can expect to pay for a half-day charter (4 hours) for a stag group of 10-12 people, departing from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina. Prices are in EUR and include skipper and fuel.

Boat typeSize (metres)Half-day cost (EUR)Full-day cost (EUR)
RIB / speedboat6-8 m1,200-1,8002,000-2,800
Sailing yacht12-15 m2,000-3,0003,500-5,000
Catamaran12-15 m2,500-3,5004,000-6,000
Motor yacht (standard)15-20 m3,000-4,5005,000-7,500
Luxury motor yacht20+ m5,000-8,0008,000-12,000+

These are guide prices. You can find cheaper deals if you book a small RIB for a short trip, or go all out on a superyacht. For a stag do, catamarans are popular because they have a large deck and are stable. Motor yachts offer more luxury and speed. Sailing yachts are slower but have a classic vibe. RIBs are good for thrill-seekers who want to go fast and do watersports. Compare options on BoatHire24 to see current availability and exact prices.

What is included in the price?

Most boat party charters in Marbella include a licensed skipper, fuel, basic safety equipment and sometimes a welcome drink or a small snack. But the devil is in the details. Always ask what is included before you book. Some operators include a cooler with ice, a sound system and a Bluetooth speaker. Others charge for these as extras. Food and drinks are almost never included in the base price, unless you book an all-inclusive package. For a stag do, you will probably want to bring your own drinks or order a catering package. Many companies allow you to bring your own alcohol, but some charge a corkage fee.

Extras that can bump up the cost: a DJ (EUR 300-600), a photographer (EUR 200-400), a barbecue or paella lunch (EUR 25-50 per person), watersports like jet skis or paddleboards (EUR 100-200 per hour), and a host or hostess. Some companies offer stag-specific packages with themed decorations, games and a dedicated party host. These can cost EUR 500-1,000 extra. Also, check if the price includes VAT (IVA in Spain, usually 10% for charters). Some operators quote without tax, which adds a surprise later. Always confirm the total price in writing.

Best departure ports for a stag boat party

Puerto Banús is the most famous marina in Marbella. It is glitzy, full of supercars and designer shops, and the boats are top-end. Stag parties love it because you can start the party at a beach club or bar before boarding. The downside is that parking and access can be chaotic in summer. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is more laid-back, with a good selection of boats and easier parking. It is also closer to Marbella old town if you want to go out after. Cabopino is quieter, with a small sandy beach nearby, good for a more relaxed vibe. Estepona and Sotogrande are further west, about 20-30 minutes drive from Marbella, but offer cheaper prices and less crowds. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, near Torremolinos, and has a large marina with many boat options.

For a stag do, Puerto Banús is the classic choice. You can step off the boat straight into the nightlife. But if you want better value, consider Marbella Marina or Estepona. The cruising area also matters. From Puerto Banús you can head towards the Cala del Faro or the coast of Estepona, with views of La Concha mountain. From Marbella Marina you can go east towards Cabopino or west towards the Río Verde. Most charters include a swim stop at a calm cove. If you want to see dolphins, head towards the Strait of Gibraltar, but that requires a longer trip and a full-day charter.

How to save money on a Marbella stag boat party

Book early, at least two to three months ahead for July and August. Last-minute bookings in peak season can be 30-50% more expensive, if you can find availability. Go for a weekday instead of a Friday or Saturday. Many operators offer discounts of 10-20% for Monday to Thursday charters. Choose a half-day instead of a full day. For a stag do, four hours is usually enough to have fun, drink, swim and take photos. If you want to save more, pick a smaller boat like a RIB or a sailing yacht rather than a luxury motor yacht. RIBs are cheaper and more fun for a group that wants speed and watersports.

Bring your own drinks and food. This can save you hundreds of euros compared to buying a catering package. Just check if the boat allows it and if there is a corkage fee. Negotiate with the charter company, especially if you are booking for a large group (12+ people). Many are willing to offer a discount or throw in extras like a free hour or a free bottle of cava. Also, consider booking through an aggregator like BoatHire24 where you can compare multiple boats and prices in one place. Finally, avoid extras you do not need. Do you really need a DJ? A Bluetooth speaker with a playlist might be just as good. Do you need a photographer? Get a friend to take photos. Every extra adds up.

What to look for in a stag boat party package

When you are comparing packages, look at the boat size and capacity. A 10-metre boat for 12 people will be cramped. Go for at least 12-15 metres for a group of 10-12. Check the deck space, you want a large sun deck or flybridge for partying. Catamarans have a wide beam and lots of deck area, making them ideal for parties. Motor yachts offer a flybridge with seating and a bar. Sailing yachts have a cockpit but less space. Also check the sound system. Some boats have a high-quality marine sound system, others have a basic radio. For a stag do, a good sound system is essential.

Ask about the skipper's experience with stag groups. Some skippers are more relaxed and party-friendly, others are strict about noise and behaviour. You want a skipper who is tolerant but also safe. Check if the boat has a toilet and a shower, essential for a day on the water. Also ask about the itinerary. Most charters will take you along the coast to a swim stop, but some allow you to choose the route. If you want to see specific places like the Cala del Faro or the Marbella skyline, mention it. Finally, read the cancellation policy. Stag dos can change at the last minute, so you want a flexible cancellation or rescheduling option. Some companies offer free cancellation up to 7 days before, others charge a fee.

Realistic budget breakdown for a stag group of 10

Let's do a rough budget for a half-day catamaran charter for 10 people in June, departing from Puerto Banús. Boat charter: EUR 3,000. Food and drinks: bring your own, EUR 200 for drinks and snacks. Extras: a Bluetooth speaker (you have one), a photographer (friend does it for free), and a swim stop (included). Total: EUR 3,200, or EUR 320 per person. If you add a DJ (EUR 500), a barbecue lunch (EUR 400 for 10 people), and a host (EUR 300), the total goes to EUR 4,400, or EUR 440 per person. For a luxury motor yacht full-day with all extras, you could be looking at EUR 8,000-10,000, or EUR 800-1,000 per person. That is a lot for a stag do, but some groups go for it.

To keep costs down, aim for EUR 250-350 per person for a half-day catamaran with basic extras. That is reasonable for Marbella. If you want a premium experience with a DJ and lunch, budget EUR 400-500 per person. For a budget option, a RIB for 3 hours with drinks and a swim stop can cost as little as EUR 1,200 total, or EUR 120 per person. That is the cheapest way to get on the water. Just remember that RIBs are small and not as comfortable for a party. If you want to see the full range of options, check out BoatHire24's blog for more tips on Marbella stag boat parties.

Common questions

How much does a Marbella boat party for a stag do cost per person? Typically EUR 120-1,000 per person depending on boat type, duration and extras. A half-day catamaran for 10 people works out at around EUR 250-350 per person.

What is the cheapest boat for a stag party in Marbella? A RIB or speedboat for 3-4 hours starts from around EUR 1,200 total for up to 10 people. That is the most budget-friendly option.

Can we bring our own alcohol on a Marbella boat party? Yes, most charter companies allow it, but some charge a corkage fee. Always confirm beforehand. Bringing your own is cheaper than buying from the boat.

Do we need a skipper for a stag boat party? Yes, all charters on BoatHire24 include a licensed skipper. You cannot rent a boat without a skipper in Spain for a group of this size.

What is the best boat type for a stag do? Catamarans are popular because they are stable and have a large deck. Motor yachts offer more luxury and speed. RIBs are good for a budget-friendly speed trip.

How far in advance should we book a stag boat party in Marbella? At least 2-3 months ahead for July and August. For May, June or September, 4-6 weeks is usually enough. Last-minute bookings are risky in peak season.

What is included in the price of a Marbella boat party? Usually a skipper, fuel, safety equipment and sometimes a welcome drink. Food, drinks, DJ, photographer and watersports are typically extra. Always check the inclusions list.

Why catamarans work best for stag groups on a budget

If you are trying to keep costs down without sacrificing space, a catamaran is your best bet. Unlike motor yachts, which burn more fuel and cost more to charter, catamarans have a wide beam that gives you a massive deck area for the same length. A 14-metre catamaran can comfortably hold 12 people partying, while a 14-metre motor yacht feels cramped with half that number. The stability is another win. No one wants to spend the day feeling seasick, especially after a few beers. Catamarans barely roll at anchor, so you can have a proper party without everyone turning green. Prices for a half-day catamaran in June start around EUR 2,500, which is often cheaper than a comparable motor yacht. For a stag group of 10, that works out to EUR 250 each before extras. You get a swim platform, a shaded cockpit, and usually a decent sound system. Just check the boat has a toilet, not all catamarans do, and that matters for a day on the water.

How to handle the deposit and payment process

Most Marbella charter companies ask for a 30-50% deposit to secure the booking, with the balance due on the day or a week before. For a EUR 3,000 charter, you are looking at EUR 900-1,500 upfront. Pay by credit card if possible, it gives you consumer protection if the company goes bust or fails to deliver. Avoid bank transfers to unknown accounts, especially for last-minute bookings. Some operators accept PayPal or Revolut, which are safer. Always get a written invoice or booking confirmation with the total price, the deposit amount, the cancellation policy, and what is included. If the company refuses to provide this, walk away. For stag groups, it is common for one person to pay the deposit and then collect money from the group. Make sure that person has a clear agreement with the others about refunds if someone drops out. A group of 10 can easily have one or two no-shows, so factor that into your budget.

What to do if the weather turns bad

Marbella gets 300 days of sunshine a year, but even in summer you can get a cloudy day or a sudden wind. The skipper has the final say on whether it is safe to go out. If the forecast is bad, most companies will offer to reschedule or give a full refund. But check the policy before you book. Some operators only refund if they cancel, not if you decide not to go. For a stag do, you might not have flexibility on the date. In that case, look for a boat with a covered deck or a cabin where you can still party if it rains. Catamarans have a large covered cockpit, motor yachts have an interior saloon. RIBs have no shelter, so avoid them if there is any chance of rain. The best months for guaranteed weather are June through September, with July and August being the most reliable. May and October can have occasional showers, but usually pass quickly. If you are booking in April or November, expect cooler temperatures around 18-22 degrees C and a higher chance of wind.

title: Marbella Boat Party for New Years Eve Dinner
excerpt: Celebrate New Year's Eve on a luxury boat in Marbella with dinner, fireworks, and a licensed skipper. A boat party for NYE dinner offers a unique way to see the Costa del Sol.
metaDescription: Book a Marbella boat party for New Year's Eve dinner. Enjoy fireworks, a luxury yacht, and a skipper. Unique NYE celebration on the Costa del Sol.
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

You can book a Marbella boat party for New Years Eve dinner that includes a private yacht or catamaran, a five-star dinner, and a front-row seat to the Puerto Banús fireworks. All charters come with a licensed skipper, so you can focus on celebrating. Prices start from around EUR 2,000 for a small group, depending on the boat size and menu.

Why a boat party beats a restaurant for NYE dinner

Restaurants in Marbella pack you in like sardines, charge EUR 500 a head, and kick you out by 2 AM. On a boat, you control the guest list, the music, and the view. You get a private space where the only queue is for the champagne. Plus, you watch the fireworks from the water, which is a lot better than craning your neck from a crowded terrace. The skipper handles the navigation, so you can drink as much as you like. BoatHire24 lists dozens of boats that include dinner packages, so you can compare options without the hard sell.

What you get with a Marbella boat party for New Years Eve dinner

A typical NYE dinner charter includes a private boat for 4-12 hours, a licensed skipper, a gourmet dinner (often with champagne and canapés), and a spot to watch the midnight fireworks. Some operators throw in a DJ or a live musician. You depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or Cabopino, and the boat anchors near the harbour for the best view of the fireworks. The dinner menu varies, but expect something like grilled sea bass, beef tenderloin, or a Spanish feast with jamón and seafood. Drinks are usually extra or part of a package. You can also add a late-night return to keep the party going until dawn. Search boats for NYE to see what's available.

Best departure ports for a NYE boat party

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice because the fireworks are right there, and the marina has a party atmosphere. But Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter and easier for parking. Cabopino offers a more relaxed vibe with a smaller crowd. Estepona has a charming old town nearby if you want to start the evening on land. Sotogrande is further west, good if you want to avoid the chaos of Banús. Benalmádena is east of Marbella, closer to Málaga airport. Each port has its own fireworks display, so you can pick based on your preferred crowd size. The boats from these ports are all within a short cruise of the fireworks, usually 10-20 minutes.

What to look for in a NYE dinner boat

Size matters. A 10-metre motor yacht works for 6-8 people, but a 15-metre catamaran is better for 12-16 guests. Check the heating: December nights on the Costa del Sol can drop to 10 degrees C, so an enclosed saloon with heating is a must. Look for a boat with a flybridge or an open deck for the fireworks, but make sure there is a warm indoor area too. Some boats come with a sound system, a TV, or even a hot tub (yes, really). The dinner should be served course by course, not a buffet that gets cold. Ask about the menu in advance, especially if you have dietary restrictions. The skipper is included, but you might want to tip them separately. Read our blog for more tips on choosing a charter boat.

Typical itinerary for a Marbella NYE boat party

Most charters start at 9 PM. You board at Puerto Banús, welcome with champagne and canapés. The boat cruises along the coast for an hour, passing the golden beaches of Marbella and the lights of La Concha mountain. Around 10:30 PM, the boat anchors near the harbour for the dinner. The starter comes out, then the main course, and dessert just before midnight. At midnight, the fireworks explode over the marina, and you toast with cava. After the fireworks, the boat either returns to port or cruises further along the coast, depending on the package. Some operators offer a 2 AM return, others let you stay out until sunrise. The skipper will adjust the route based on wind and sea conditions, but the plan is always to give you the best view.

Cost of a Marbella boat party for New Years Eve dinner

Prices vary wildly. A basic motor yacht for 6 people with a simple dinner might cost from around EUR 2,000. A luxury catamaran for 16 guests with a full gourmet menu and open bar can be EUR 8,000 or more. Superyachts are price on request, but expect five figures. The cost includes the boat, skipper, fuel, and dinner. Drinks are often extra unless you book an open bar package. You can save by booking early: November prices are usually 20% lower than last-minute December bookings. Compare prices on BoatHire24 to find the best deal for your group size and budget.

What to wear and bring on a NYE boat party

Dress for the evening: smart casual is fine, but some people go full black tie. Bring a jacket or a pashmina because it gets chilly on deck after sunset. Non-slip shoes are a good idea, especially if you plan to dance. You can bring your own decorations, but check with the skipper first. Some boats allow balloons and banners, others don't. A small gift for the skipper is a nice touch, but not required. Don't forget your camera for the fireworks. If you plan to swim (unlikely in December), bring a towel. The boat will have life jackets, but you won't need them unless you are on a RIB.

Local colour: what makes Marbella special for NYE

Marbella in December is mild compared to northern Europe. You can sit on deck in a sweater and enjoy the sea breeze. The fireworks in Puerto Banús are famous, with a 10-minute display that lights up the entire marina. The mountains behind the coast, especially La Concha, add a dramatic backdrop. After the party, you can walk through the port and see the superyachts decked out in lights. Estepona old town has a charming Christmas market if you want to extend your stay. The Strait of Gibraltar is a bit far for a NYE cruise, but you might see dolphins on the way back if you head west. For a truly unique experience, some boats offer a midnight cruise to the Cabo de Gata lighthouse, but that is a longer trip.

Common questions

Can I book a boat for a small group of 4 people? Yes, many motor yachts and RIBs are available for 4-6 guests. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a basic package.

Is the skipper included in the price? Yes, every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. You do not need a boating licence.

What if the weather is bad on NYE? The skipper will decide if it is safe to sail. Most boats have a heated saloon, so you can still enjoy the fireworks from inside. If the trip is cancelled, you get a full refund.

Can I bring my own food and drinks? Some operators allow it, but most NYE packages include dinner and drinks. Check the terms before booking.

How far in advance should I book? Book at least 2-3 months ahead for NYE. Popular boats sell out by November.

Are children allowed on NYE boat parties? Yes, but check with the operator. Some boats have age restrictions for safety reasons.

What happens after midnight? Most charters return to port by 1 AM, but you can extend the trip for an extra fee. Some boats offer a sunrise return.

How to choose between a motor yacht and a catamaran for NYE dinner

Motor yachts are faster, so you can cover more coastline before dinner. A 15-metre Sunseeker or Princess will get you from Puerto Banús to Cabopino in 20 minutes, giving you a longer sunset cruise. Catamarans are more stable, which matters if anyone in your group gets queasy. They also have more deck space, so a 12-metre Lagoon feels roomier than a 12-metre motor yacht. For dinner, catamarans often have a proper dining table on the aft deck, whereas motor yachts might serve dinner in a saloon. If you want to dance, a motor yacht with a flybridge gives you a separate area. Catamarans are better for groups who want to sit together and eat. Either way, check the boat's heating and enclosed spaces. A flybridge at 10 degrees C in December is only fun for the first five minutes.

What the dinner menu looks like on a typical NYE charter

Most operators offer a set menu, not a la carte. A common starter is a seafood platter with prawns, oysters, and crab claws. The main course is usually a choice of grilled sea bass with roasted vegetables or beef tenderloin with truffle mash. Dessert is often a chocolate fondant or a Spanish cheesecake. Some boats include a midnight snack of churros with chocolate. Drinks packages range from EUR 50 to EUR 150 per person for champagne, wine, beer, and spirits. If you want a vegan or vegetarian menu, ask in advance: most skippers can arrange it, but they need notice. The dinner is served course by course, usually by a steward or the skipper. Buffet dinners are cheaper but less elegant. For a group of 10, expect the dinner to take about 90 minutes from starter to dessert.

Why Cabopino is an underrated departure port for NYE

Cabopino is a small marina east of Marbella, near the dunes of Artola. It has a quieter crowd than Puerto Banús, but the fireworks are still impressive. The marina has a few restaurants and a beach bar, but nothing like the chaos of Banús. If you want a more intimate party with your group, Cabopino is a good choice. The boats here are smaller on average, mostly motor yachts and catamarans up to 14 metres. You can anchor near the Cabopino beach for the fireworks, which are launched from the marina pier. The water is calm here because the marina is sheltered by a breakwater. Parking is easier than Banús, and you can walk from the car to the boat in five minutes. The only downside is fewer nightlife options after the party, but your boat can take you to Banús if you want to continue.

How to handle dietary restrictions on a NYE boat dinner

Most operators can accommodate gluten-free, dairy-free, or nut-free diets, but you need to tell them at least a week in advance. For vegan menus, ask for a separate vegan starter and main, like a roasted vegetable tart or a mushroom risotto. Halal and kosher meals are harder to find on boats in Marbella, but some skippers can source them from local caterers. If you have a serious allergy, bring your own EpiPen and tell the skipper. The boat's galley is small, so cross-contamination is possible. For groups with mixed diets, the easiest option is a tapas-style dinner with multiple small dishes. That way everyone can pick what they want. Avoid buffets if you have allergies, because guests can mix serving spoons. Always confirm the menu in writing before you pay.

The best time to book a NYE boat party for the best price

Book between September and October for the lowest prices. Operators often offer early-bird discounts of 15-20% off the standard rate. By November, the popular boats start to fill up, and prices rise. December bookings are usually at full price, and you might struggle to find availability for groups larger than 10. If you wait until the week before NYE, you might find last-minute cancellations, but that is a gamble. The best value is a 6-8 person motor yacht booked in October, from around EUR 2,000. For a catamaran with 12-14 guests, book by October to secure a rate under EUR 4,000. Superyachts are price on request, but early booking gives you more negotiating power. Remember that deposits are usually 50% non-refundable, so make sure your group is confirmed before you pay.

What happens if someone gets seasick on NYE

The Costa del Sol is usually calm in December, with wave heights under 1 metre. But if the wind picks up, a motor yacht at anchor can roll a bit. Catamarans are more stable, so they are better for queasy guests. Most boats have a saloon with sofas where you can lie down. The skipper will have seasickness tablets on board, but bring your own if you know you are sensitive. Avoid heavy meals before boarding. Stick to the deck for fresh air, and look at the horizon. If someone is really sick, the skipper can return to port early, but that ruins the evening for everyone. Better to take a ginger tablet or a Scopoderm patch before you leave. Alcohol makes seasickness worse, so pace yourself on the champagne.

How to decorate your NYE boat party

Most operators allow decorations as long as they do not damage the boat. Avoid confetti, glitter, or anything that leaves a mess. Balloons are fine, but use biodegradable ones. String lights or battery-powered fairy lights add a festive touch without risk. Some boats have a sound system, so you can play your own playlist. Check if the boat has a Bluetooth speaker or AUX input. If you want a DJ, ask the operator in advance; some can arrange one for an extra fee. For the dinner table, bring a small centrepiece, but nothing that can tip over in a swell. No candles on deck because of the wind. Battery-operated LED candles are safer. If you want a photo backdrop, use a simple banner or a foil curtain. The skipper will tell you where you can hang things.

What to do after the fireworks if you want to keep partying

Some charters include a post-midnight cruise to the Marbella coastline, with the boat lit up and music playing. You can anchor near the Marbella Club or the Golden Mile and watch the lights from the shore. Other boats return to Puerto Banús by 1 AM, where the marina bars and clubs stay open until 6 AM. Popular spots are Pangea, Aqwa Mist, and La Suite. If you are in Cabopino, the beach bars close earlier, so you might need a taxi to Banús. For a truly extended party, some operators offer a sunrise cruise that leaves at 6 AM and returns at 9 AM. That costs extra, from around EUR 500 for a small boat. You can also book a hotel room nearby, like the Marbella Club or Puente Romano, to sleep it off before breakfast.

Why a RIB or speedboat is a bad idea for NYE dinner

RIBs and speedboats are open, with no cabin or heating. At 10 degrees C at night, you will freeze. They also have no toilet, no galley, and no table for dinner. The ride is bumpy, so you cannot serve a proper meal. RIBs are fine for a daytime trip to Cala del Faro, but not for a formal dinner. If you want a small, cheap option, look for a 6-metre motor yacht with a small cabin instead. Even a 7-metre Bayliner with a cuddy cabin is better than a RIB. The minimum for a comfortable NYE dinner is an 8-metre boat with an enclosed saloon. If your group is only 4 people, a 9-metre motor yacht is perfect. Do not compromise on comfort for the sake of a lower price. You will regret it when the wind picks up.

How to split the cost among a group for a NYE boat party

Most operators charge a flat rate for the boat, not per person. For a EUR 3,000 charter with 6 people, that is EUR 500 each. With 10 people, it drops to EUR 300 each. Drinks are usually extra, so factor in EUR 50-100 per person for an open bar. If you want a DJ, add another EUR 200-400 split across the group. The easiest way to collect money is to use a payment app like Splitwise or PayPal. Ask everyone to pay their share before the deposit is due. If someone cancels, you need a backup plan. Some operators allow you to reduce the group size up to 14 days before, but you still pay the flat rate. So make sure everyone is committed before you book.
