title: Hen Do Boat Fuengirola: Fun Packages
excerpt: Planning a hen do in Fuengirola? A private boat charter with a skipper is the ultimate way to celebrate. Sun, sea, and sangria on the Costa del Sol.
metaDescription: Hen do boat Fuengirola: book a private charter with skipper, sun decks, and party vibes. Compare boats from EUR 250. Start the celebration on the water.
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

If you are organising a hen do in Fuengirola and want something that doesn't involve queuing for a club or fighting for a sunbed, a private boat charter is your move. You get a whole boat, a licensed skipper who does the navigating, and you can bring your own drinks, food, and playlist. Depart from Fuengirola port or nearby Puerto Banús, cruise the Costa del Sol coastline, stop for a swim, and return with a tan and some questionable photos. Prices for a half-day charter start from around EUR 250 for a smaller boat, and you can go up to a luxury yacht for the full VIP treatment. No boating licence needed, no hidden costs, just you, your mates, and the Mediterranean.

Why a boat beats a bar for a hen do

You have done the sticky-floored club thing, the bottomless brunch that runs out of bubbles after 90 minutes, and the paintball session that left you with bruises you couldn't explain. A hen do boat Fuengirola flips the script. You get a private space where you control the music (yes, that means you can play the bride-to-be's guilty pleasure on repeat), the drinks, and the itinerary. No one tells you to leave at 2am because the venue is closing. You anchor in a quiet cove, jump off the bow, and float in the warm Mediterranean. The skipper handles the boat, so you can focus on being the world's best bridesmaid (or maid of honour, we are not judging). Plus, the backdrop for photos is unbeatable: the Sierra Blanca mountains behind you, the sea in front, and the Marbella coastline stretching out to the west.

What you get with a hen do boat charter

When you book a hen do boat Fuengirola through BoatHire24, you are not just renting a vessel. Every charter includes a licensed skipper who knows the local waters, the best swimming spots, and where to find the dolphins if they are playing ball. You get the boat for your chosen time slot, typically 4, 6, or 8 hours. Most boats come with a sound system (Bluetooth, so your Spotify playlist works), a sun deck for lounging, a shaded area for when the sun gets too much, and a small fridge or cool box for drinks. You can bring your own food and drink, or arrange a catering package through the boat owner. Some boats have a barbecue on the back deck. Others have a slide or a paddleboard. The key is to pick a boat that fits your group size. A standard motor yacht for 10-12 people costs from around EUR 250 for a half day. A larger catamaran for 20+ will be more, but the per-person cost stays reasonable.

Best departure ports for a Fuengirola hen do

Fuengirola has its own marina, Puerto Deportivo de Fuengirola, which is a solid choice for a hen do boat Fuengirola. It is central, easy to get to by taxi or train (Fuengirola train station is a 10-minute walk from the port), and there are plenty of bars and restaurants nearby for pre- or post-cruise drinks. But you are not limited to Fuengirola. Puerto Banús, 15 minutes up the coast, is the glitzier option if you want to start the day with a champagne breakfast overlooking superyachts. Cabopino, just east of Fuengirola, is quieter and has a lovely dune-backed beach. Estepona, a bit further west, offers a more laid-back vibe with its old town and flower-filled streets. Benalmádena, to the east, is another option with a large marina and plenty of nightlife. Each port gives you a different start to your hen do, but all offer easy access to the same beautiful coastline.

Types of boats for a hen do in Fuengirola

Your hen do boat Fuengirola options break down into a few main categories. Motor yachts are the most popular for hen dos. They are sleek, have plenty of deck space, and can get you to the swimming spots quickly. A 10-metre motor yacht with a sun pad on the bow is ideal for 8-12 people. Catamarans are great for larger groups because they have more deck area and are more stable (less seasickness, more dancing). A 14-metre catamaran can take 20-30 people comfortably. Sailing yachts offer a more relaxed, classic experience, but the heeling can be a problem if you are wearing heels. RIBs and speedboats are for the adrenaline crowd: you can tow a ringo or just blast along the coast. Licence-free day boats are a newer option: small, simple boats you can drive yourself without a licence, but for a hen do you probably want the skipper so you can all drink. Superyachts are available for the budget-is-no-object group, with crews, chefs, and all the trimmings.

What to bring and what to expect

For a hen do boat Fuengirola, you need to pack strategically. Sun cream (factor 50, the Spanish sun does not mess about), sunglasses, a hat, a towel, and a change of clothes for later. Swimwear is mandatory. Shoes: barefoot or non-marking soles on deck, so leave the stilettos at the port. Drinks: bring your own or arrange a drinks package. Most boats have a cool box, but check the size. Food: easy stuff like sandwiches, fruit, crisps, and cake. Some boats have a barbecue, but confirm in advance. Music: download your playlist to your phone because signal can be patchy offshore. The skipper will give you a safety briefing at the start. You will likely stop at a beach or cove for a swim: Cala del Faro near Marbella or the beaches around Cabopino are popular. Some charters include a stop at a beach club for lunch or drinks, but that is extra. The skipper will be back at the port at the agreed time, so plan your post-cruise activities accordingly.

How to book a hen do boat in Fuengirola

Booking a hen do boat Fuengirola is straightforward on BoatHire24's search page. Enter Fuengirola as the departure port, your group size, and the date. The site shows available boats with prices, photos, and details. You can filter by boat type, price range, and amenities. Once you find a boat you like, send an enquiry or book directly online. The owner or skipper will confirm the booking and send you the meeting point details. Payment is usually a deposit to secure the date, with the balance due on the day. Make sure you read the cancellation policy: most require 48-72 hours notice for a full refund. For a hen do, book at least two weeks in advance, especially in July and August when boats go fast. If you are unsure, contact the BoatHire24 team for recommendations.

Costs and what affects the price

The price of a hen do boat Fuengirola depends on several factors. Boat size and type are the biggest: a small motor yacht for 10 people might cost from EUR 250 for a half day, while a large catamaran for 30 people can be EUR 800 or more. Time of year matters: July and August are peak season and prices are higher. Booking for a full day (8 hours) costs more than a half day (4 hours), but you get more time to enjoy the coast. Extras add up: catering, drinks packages, water toys (paddleboards, ringos), and beach club stops all cost extra. Some boats charge a cleaning fee if you make a mess. Fuel is usually included in the price for local cruising, but if you want to go further, there may be a fuel surcharge. The skipper's gratuity is not included: 10-15% of the charter fee is standard if you are happy with the service.

Local tips for a Fuengirola hen do on the water

Fuengirola has a year-round temperate climate, but the best months for a hen do boat Fuengirola are May to October. Water temperatures hit 22-26 degrees C from June to September. Start your charter in the morning (10am) to get the calmest sea conditions and the best light for photos. If you want to see dolphins, head towards the Strait of Gibraltar area, but that is a longer trip from Fuengirola. Closer to home, the waters off Cabopino and the Costa del Sol often have bottlenose dolphins. For a lunch stop, consider a beach club like Nikki Beach or Ocean Club in Marbella, but book ahead and expect to pay for a table. If you want a quieter spot, anchor off the coast of Estepona and swim ashore to a chiringuito. Avoid the afternoon heat by having a shaded area on the boat. And remember: the bride-to-be does not have to do anything she does not want to. It is her day.

Common questions

Do we need a boating licence for a hen do boat Fuengirola? No. Every charter through BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles the boat. You just turn up and enjoy.

How many people can we bring? It depends on the boat. Small motor yachts take 8-12 people. Catamarans can take 20-30 or more. Check the boat's capacity on the listing.

Can we bring our own drinks? Yes, most boats allow you to bring your own food and drink. Some have a corkage fee if you use their glassware. Check with the owner in advance.

What happens if the weather is bad? The skipper decides if it is safe to go out. If the charter is cancelled due to weather, you get a full refund or can reschedule. If you cancel for other reasons, the policy varies.

Is there a toilet on board? Most motor yachts and catamarans have a marine toilet. Smaller RIBs and speedboats may not. Check the boat description.

Can we play our own music? Yes, almost all boats have a Bluetooth sound system. Bring your phone with a downloaded playlist.

How far in advance should we book? At least two weeks, especially in summer. Popular boats book up quickly. For last-minute bookings, check the site for availability.

What is the best time of day for a hen do boat trip? Morning (10am-2pm) for calm seas and good light. Afternoon (2pm-6pm) for sunbathing and sunset. Evening charters (6pm-10pm) for a sunset party vibe.

How to handle a hen do with mixed mobility or seasickness

Not everyone in the group will have sea legs or the ability to scramble up a ladder from the water. For a hen do boat Fuengirola, pick a catamaran if anyone is prone to seasickness. Catamarans are more stable because they have two hulls, so the rocking motion is much less than on a monohull motor yacht. If you have someone with limited mobility, look for a boat with a wide boarding ramp and a main deck that is flush with the cockpit. Avoid boats with steep steps down to a cabin or a high bow that requires climbing over seats. Bring seasickness tablets anyway: the pharmacist in Fuengirola sells Biodramina for a few euros. Take them 30 minutes before departure. And if someone does feel queasy, the skipper can head to calmer waters closer to the shore. The area between Fuengirola and Cabopino is usually flat in the morning.

Hen do boat Fuengirola: what to do if it rains or the sea is rough

July and August are almost guaranteed sunshine, but May, June, September, and October can throw up a cloudy day or a short thunderstorm. If the weather looks iffy, your skipper will make the call. If the charter is cancelled due to unsafe conditions, you get a full refund or can reschedule. But if it is just a bit cloudy with no wind, the trip goes ahead. Bring a light jacket or a hoodie for the breeze. If the sea is choppy, the skipper will avoid open water and stick to the coastline between Fuengirola and Marbella, which is more sheltered. You can still swim in a sheltered cove like Cala del Faro. The worst case is a day of rain and wind: in that case, reschedule. Most boat owners are flexible if you give them 24 hours notice. Do not risk a hen do in bad weather; it is not fun being wet and cold on a boat.

Hen do boat Fuengirola: what to do after the charter

The boat drops you back at the port, but the night is young. If you depart from Puerto Deportivo de Fuengirola, you are a 5-minute walk from the main strip of bars and clubs on Paseo Marítimo. Try La Cueva for a lively bar or Mango Club for dancing. If you want a sit-down meal, the port has several seafood restaurants like Restaurante El Sardinero. If you left from Puerto Banús, the party continues at Pangea or the beach clubs. For a quieter evening, head to Estepona old town and eat at a terrace restaurant on the Plaza de las Flores. If you have a designated driver or are getting taxis, plan ahead: taxis in Fuengirola are cheap (around EUR 10-15 to most hotels), but they can be scarce after midnight. Uber works in the area too. And if the bride-to-be is exhausted, just get a pizza and go to bed. It is her hen do, not a military operation.

Hen do boat Fuengirola: how to save money without spoiling the fun

A hen do boat Fuengirola does not have to break the bank. The biggest saving is to book a half-day (4 hours) instead of a full day. You still get time for a swim, drinks, and a cruise, but you pay roughly half the price. Book on a weekday (Monday to Thursday) and you can save 20-30% compared to a weekend. Choose a smaller boat: a 10-metre motor yacht for 8-10 people is cheaper than a 15-metre catamaran for 20. Bring your own drinks and food instead of ordering a catering package. Buy the drinks at Mercadona or Carrefour in Fuengirola: a bottle of cava costs EUR 3, a litre of gin is EUR 10. Skip the beach club lunch stop; anchor at a quiet cove and have a picnic. If you want water toys, a paddleboard costs around EUR 40-50 extra, but you can just swim for free. Split the cost equally among the group, including the bride. Most groups do that anyway.

Hen do boat Fuengirola: what to do if someone gets too drunk

It happens. Someone overdoes it on the cava or the sun hits them harder than expected. On a hen do boat Fuengirola, the skipper is responsible for safety. If someone is clearly intoxicated and a danger to themselves or others, the skipper can end the charter early and return to port. That ruins the day for everyone. So set some ground rules before you board. Alternate alcoholic drinks with water. Eat proper food, not just crisps. Use sun cream and reapply it. If someone does get too drunk, keep them in the shade, give them water, and do not let them near the edge of the boat. The skipper will have a first aid kit and can call the coastguard if needed. But honestly, most skippers are used to hen dos and will keep an eye on things. Just do not be that group that gets kicked off the boat.

Hen do boat Fuengirola: how to get the best photos and videos

Your hen do boat Fuengirola will generate content for weeks. The best light for photos is the golden hour: the first hour after sunrise and the last hour before sunset. If you book a morning charter (10am-2pm), the light is bright but not harsh. For a sunset charter (6pm-10pm), you get warm tones and long shadows. Tell the skipper you want a photo stop near the coast with the Sierra Blanca mountains in the background. The area off Cabopino has a great view of the dunes and the sea. Bring a waterproof phone case or a GoPro for swimming shots. A selfie stick is fine, but a drone is not allowed without permission from the boat owner. For group shots, have everyone stand on the bow facing the sun. For a candid shot, catch the bride laughing while holding a cava bottle. And do not forget a group shot at the end with the boat name visible. That is the classic hen do photo.

title: Stag Do Boat Fuengirola: Adventure Awaits
excerpt: Forget sticky-floored clubs. A stag do boat in Fuengirola gives you sun, sea, a private bar, and a skipper who knows where the dolphins hang out. No hangover required, but it helps.
metaDescription: Plan the ultimate stag do boat Fuengirola trip. Private yacht, skipper, booze, and dolphins. Book your lads' charter on the Costa del Sol today.
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

If you are organising a stag do in Fuengirola and want something that doesn't involve a sticky carpet and a 4 a.m. kebab, get a private boat. You get a licensed skipper, a sound system that actually works, unlimited sun, and a cooler full of whatever the groom-to-be demands. Depart from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina, cruise past the Sierra Blanca, anchor off a quiet cove, and let the groom jump off the bow. Costs run from around EUR 80 per person for a half-day on a motor yacht, all in. No hidden fees, no hangover.

Why Fuengirola works for a stag boat trip

Fuengirola sits right on the Costa del Sol strip, 30 minutes from Marbella and 20 from Benalmádena. The coastline here is a mix of sandy beaches, rocky coves, and the odd cliff that looks like it was designed for a cannonball competition. The water is calm from May to October, sea temps hit 24 degrees C in August, and the wind rarely blows hard enough to cancel a trip.

You can launch from Fuengirola port itself, but most stag groups prefer Puerto Banús because it has more yacht options and the bars are open before you even step aboard. The trip from Banús to Fuengirola takes about 40 minutes on a 30-knot motor yacht, giving you time to crack the first beer and let the groom pick the playlist.

What makes Fuengirola better than, say, Benalmádena for a stag? The town itself has a proper nightlife strip, but the real draw is the water. You get the Sierra de Mijas mountains as a backdrop, the occasional pod of common dolphins near Cala del Faro, and a coastline that changes from marina to wild cliff in less than a mile. No other stag destination on the Costa del Sol gives you that mix of convenience and raw coast.

What you actually get on a stag do boat in Fuengirola

Every charter on BoatHire24 comes with a licensed skipper. That is not optional. You do not need a licence, you do not need to know how to tie a cleat hitch, and you definitely do not need to worry about parking the thing. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring, and the safety briefing. You handle the ice, the music, and the group photos.

Most boats for stag groups are motor yachts between 10 m and 18 m. A 12 m Sunseeker or Azimut holds 10 to 12 people comfortably. Catamarans are also popular because they have more deck space and a lower centre of gravity, which means less seasickness for the lads who had one too many the night before. RIBs and speedboats work for smaller groups who want to go fast, but they lack the shade and the toilet that a yacht provides.

Standard inclusions on a half-day charter (4 hours):
- Licensed skipper and fuel
- Onboard sound system (Bluetooth or AUX)
- Cooler with ice (you bring the drinks)
- Snorkelling gear and paddleboard if you ask
- Insurance and safety equipment
- Pick-up and drop-off at the same port

Exclusions: food, drinks (unless you pre-order a catering package), and any damage from the groom falling off the bow. That last one is on you.

Best boats for a stag group: size, speed, and style

You do not need a superyacht for a stag do, but you do need enough deck space so that no one is sitting on the engine hatch. Here is a rough guide based on group size:

Group sizeRecommended boat typeLength (m)Typical speed (kts)Price range (half-day)
6-8RIB or speedboat6-830-40EUR 500-800
8-12Motor yacht10-1420-30EUR 800-1,500
12-16Catamaran12-168-15EUR 1,200-2,000
16-20Large motor yacht16-2018-25EUR 2,000-3,500

Prices are estimates and vary by season and boat model. Contact the owner directly via BoatHire24 search for exact quotes.

For a stag do, the sweet spot is a 12 m motor yacht. Fast enough to cover ground, stable enough to stand on while drinking, and with a cabin where at least one person can sleep off the effects of the pre-departure shots.

Itinerary ideas: from lazy cruise to full-on party

You can keep it simple or go big. Here are three itineraries that work for stag groups departing from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina.

Option 1: The lazy cruise (4 hours)
Depart at 11 a.m., head east towards Cabopino. Anchor off Cala del Faro, a rocky cove with clear water and no crowds. Swim, snorkel, paddleboard. Lunch is a picnic on deck or a beach stop. Back by 3 p.m. for a siesta before the evening session. Cost: from EUR 80 per person.

Option 2: The dolphin run (6 hours)
Depart at 10 a.m., head west towards Estepona and the Strait of Gibraltar. Common dolphins and pilot whales are frequent sightings between June and September. Stop for lunch at a chiringuito in Estepona old town, then cruise back via the Punta de la Doncella lighthouse. Back by 4 p.m. Cost: from EUR 120 per person.

Option 3: The full-day party (8 hours)
Depart at 10 a.m., head to Benalmádena or even as far as Nerja if the sea is flat. Anchor in a secluded bay, crank the sound system, and do the stag challenges (swimming trunks on the mast, belly flop contest, groom speech). Lunch is a barbecue on board or a stop at a beach club. Back by 6 p.m. Cost: from EUR 180 per person.

All itineraries include the skipper. You do not need to navigate. You just need to show up with the groom and a sense of humour.

What to bring and what to leave at the hotel

Bring: swimwear, towel, sunscreen (factor 50, the sun here burns through clouds), sunglasses, a hat, a change of clothes for after, a waterproof phone case, and your own drinks if the boat does not include a catering package. A Bluetooth speaker is redundant if the boat has its own system, but bring one as backup if the group is large.

Leave: glass bottles (most skippers ban them for safety), high heels (you will ruin the deck and your ankles), anything that cannot get wet, and the groom's wedding ring if he plans to jump off the bow. You have been warned.

If you want food, pre-order a catering package from the boat owner. Most offer Spanish platters (jamón, cheese, olives, bread) for around EUR 15-25 per person. Some allow you to bring your own barbecue on catamarans with a gas grill. Ask the owner before you book.

When to go: season, weather, and sea conditions

The Costa del Sol has a Mediterranean climate with 300 days of sun a year. The best months for a stag do boat trip are May through October. May and June are warm but not scorching (25-28 degrees C), July and August are hot (30-35 degrees C) and crowded, September is still warm (28 degrees C) with fewer tourists, and October is mild (22-25 degrees C) and often calm.

Sea conditions: the Mediterranean is generally flat in summer, with swell rarely above 0.5 m. The Levante wind can pick up in the afternoon, especially near Gibraltar, but skippers monitor forecasts and will adjust the itinerary. If the wind is strong, they will anchor in a sheltered cove rather than risk a bumpy ride.

Rain: almost none from June to August. September and October can have the odd shower, but it usually passes in 20 minutes. You are safe booking any day from May to mid-October.

How to book a stag do boat in Fuengirola without getting ripped off

Book through BoatHire24 because we list verified boats with real photos, clear pricing, and direct contact with the owner. Avoid third-party agents who add a 20-30% markup and then disappear when the boat breaks down.

Steps:
1. Go to the search page and filter by port (Fuengirola, Puerto Banús, or Marbella Marina).
2. Choose a boat that matches your group size. Read the description and check the photos for deck space, shade, and toilet.
3. Message the owner directly via the platform. Ask about availability, catering, and any restrictions (some owners do not allow glass or red wine).
4. Pay a deposit (usually 30-50%) to secure the date. Balance is paid on the day.
5. Confirm the meeting point and time. Most boats depart from the port's main dock at 10 a.m. or 2 p.m. for half-day trips.

What to watch out for: owners who demand full payment upfront, boats that look nothing like the photos, and skippers who do not speak English (most do, but check). Also, confirm that the boat has a marine toilet. You do not want the groom to have to hold it in for four hours.

Common questions

Can we bring our own alcohol on board?

Yes, most owners allow you to bring your own drinks. Some charge a corkage fee if you bring glass bottles, so use plastic or cans. Ask the owner before you book.

Do we need a boat licence?

No. Every charter includes a licensed skipper who handles the boat. You just relax and enjoy.

What if someone gets seasick?

Tell them to take a seasickness tablet 30 minutes before departure. The skipper can also anchor in a sheltered cove if the sea is choppy. Catamarans are more stable than motor yachts.

Can we swim and snorkel?

Yes. Most boats carry snorkelling gear and paddleboards. The skipper will anchor in a safe spot for swimming. Just do not dive off the bow without checking the depth.

What happens if the weather is bad?

The skipper decides if it is safe to sail. If the trip is cancelled due to weather, you get a full refund or a reschedule. If you cancel last minute for non-weather reasons, you lose the deposit.

Is there a toilet on board?

Most motor yachts and catamarans over 10 m have a marine toilet. RIBs and speedboats usually do not. Check the boat description or ask the owner.

Can we play our own music?

Yes. Most boats have a Bluetooth or AUX sound system. Bring your own playlist and a backup speaker if the group is large.

Puerto Banús vs Marbella Marina: which departure port suits your stag

Puerto Banús is the obvious choice for a stag do boat Fuengirola trip because it is the flashiest port on the Costa del Sol. You get the superyacht row, the designer shops, and the bars where the groom can buy his first round before you even leave the dock. The downside is parking. If anyone drives, expect to pay EUR 30-50 for a day in the underground car park. The upside is that every boat owner in Banús knows how to handle a stag group. They have seen it all.

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) is quieter, cheaper to park (EUR 15-20), and still has a few decent bars on the waterfront. The boats are slightly older on average, but the prices are lower. A 12 m motor yacht from Marbella Marina might cost EUR 900 for a half-day versus EUR 1,200 from Banús. The cruising time to Fuengirola is the same from both ports, about 40 minutes at 25 knots. The key difference is the vibe. Banús is for the group that wants to be seen. Marbella Marina is for the group that wants to save EUR 300 and spend it on more drinks.

Either way, you end up in the same water. The Sierra Blanca mountains, the clear coves, and the dolphins do not care which port you left from. Book whichever fits your budget and your tolerance for Lamborghinis parked outside the marina cafe.

How to keep the groom alive and the deposit safe

Every stag do boat Fuengirola charter comes with a damage deposit, usually EUR 500-1,000 held on a credit card. The owner releases it if the boat comes back in the same condition. Here is how to avoid losing it. First, ban glass bottles. They break, they cut feet, and they cost you EUR 50 per broken bottle in cleaning fees. Bring cans or plastic. Second, no red wine. Spill it on the white upholstery and you are looking at a EUR 200 cleaning charge. Stick to beer, gin and tonic, or white wine spritzers.

Third, keep the groom away from the helm. He will want to steer the boat. The skipper will probably let him for 30 seconds. That is fine. But if he tries to rev the engines or turn the wheel hard, the skipper will shut it down. Do not argue. The skipper has a licence to protect and a boat to return. Fourth, do not let anyone jump off the bow unless the skipper confirms the depth. A 3 m jump into 1.5 m of water is a broken ankle. A 5 m jump into 0.5 m is a broken spine. The skipper knows the spots. Trust them.

Finally, clean up before you dock. Collect the cans, the food wrappers, and any stray clothing. The owner will do a quick inspection. If the deck is tidy and nothing is broken, you get the deposit back. Simple.

Why a catamaran beats a motor yacht for a large stag group

If your stag do boat Fuengirola group is 12 or more, a catamaran is the better choice. Motor yachts have a V-shaped hull that rolls in any swell. Catamarans have two hulls and a wide beam, so they sit flat even when the sea kicks up. That means less seasickness, more stable deck for dancing, and more space to spread out. A 14 m catamaran has roughly the same deck area as an 18 m motor yacht. You get a trampoline net at the bow where people can lie in the sun, a shaded cockpit with seating for everyone, and usually two toilets instead of one.

The trade-off is speed. A catamaran cruises at 8-12 knots, half the speed of a motor yacht. The trip from Puerto Banús to Fuengirola takes 45 minutes instead of 20. But for a stag do, speed is not the priority. You are not trying to get anywhere fast. You are trying to anchor in a cove, drink, swim, and repeat. The catamaran does that better because it draws less water, so it can anchor closer to the beach. You can step off the bow into waist-deep water without a ladder.

Cost wise, a 14 m catamaran for a half-day runs from EUR 1,200-1,800, split 12 ways that is EUR 100-150 per person. For a motor yacht of the same capacity, you pay EUR 1,000-1,500, or EUR 83-125 per person. The catamaran is slightly more expensive but worth it for the stability and the space. Ask the owner if the trampoline net is load-rated for adults. Some are not.

What to do if someone cannot swim on a stag do boat Fuengirola

It happens. One of the lads never learned, or he is too hungover to trust his coordination. The skipper will provide life jackets for everyone on board. They are mandatory for children under 12 and recommended for anyone who is not a strong swimmer. Put the non-swimmer in a life jacket before the boat leaves the dock. Do not wait until they are in the water.

If the group wants to swim, the skipper will anchor in a spot where the depth is 3-5 m and the current is minimal. The non-swimmer can stay on the boat or use a paddleboard as a float. Most boats carry at least one paddleboard. Tie a line to it so it does not drift. Or just let them sit on the deck with a drink and watch the others act like idiots. That is a valid stag role.

One practical tip: tell the non-swimmer to avoid the bow jump. A belly flop from 3 m hurts even if you can swim. From 5 m, it can knock the wind out of you. If they insist on jumping, make sure they wear the life jacket and jump feet first. The skipper will have a word if they try a cannonball. Trust the skipper.

How to handle the stag challenges on a boat without getting banned

Every stag do boat Fuengirola group wants to do something stupid. The question is whether the owner will let you. Most owners are fine with belly flop contests, groom speeches, and the occasional inflatable flamingo. They are not fine with anything that damages the boat, endangers people, or involves throwing someone off the flybridge. Check the charter terms before you book. Some owners explicitly forbid stag groups. Others welcome them and have a list of dos and don'ts.

Safe challenges that work on a boat: best belly flop (judged by the skipper), longest underwater swim (timed), worst dance move to the boat's sound system, and a groom quiz where he has to answer questions about his fiancée while balancing on a paddleboard. Avoid challenges that involve climbing the mast (the rigging is not a climbing frame), jumping between boats (the gap is always wider than it looks), or drinking games that lead to someone vomiting over the side (the owner will charge you for cleaning the deck).

If you want to do a themed dress code, keep it simple. Hawaiian shirts, inflatable costumes, or matching swim trunks. Do not bring anything with glitter. Glitter gets into the upholstery and never comes out. The owner will remember your group. Not in a good way.

Why September is the best month for a stag do boat Fuengirola

May and June are warm, but the sea is still cool (18-20 degrees C). July and August are hot and crowded, with marinas full of families and a 30% premium on boat prices. September is the sweet spot. The sea hits 24 degrees C, the air is 28-30 degrees C, the tourist crowds thin out after the first week, and the boat prices drop by 15-20% compared to August. You get the same sun, the same calm water, and fewer people fighting for space at the anchorages.

The evenings are still warm enough for dinner on a terrace, and the stag night after the boat trip is less chaotic because the town is not packed with British families. The only risk is the occasional September shower, but they pass quickly. Check the forecast 48 hours before and have a backup plan. The skipper will not sail in a thunderstorm, but a light shower is fine. Bring a waterproof jacket and keep the music playing.

Cost wise, a half-day motor yacht in September averages EUR 800-1,200 for 10 people, or EUR 80-120 per person. In July, the same boat is EUR 1,000-1,500. That saving covers the catering package and a round of drinks at the marina bar afterwards. Book early September, not late. The first two weeks are the best. After the 15th, the wind can pick up as autumn approaches.

title: Hen Do Boat Estepona: Coastal Celebration
excerpt: Planning a hen do in Estepona? Hire a boat with a skipper for a day of sun, sea, and celebration. Motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs available from Puerto Banús and Marbella.
metaDescription: Find the perfect hen do boat Estepona for your coastal celebration. Motor yachts, catamarans, and RIBs with skipper. Book now for sun, sea, and sangria.
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

You want a hen do that doesn't involve a sticky-floored nightclub and a hangover the size of La Concha mountain. Hire a boat in Estepona. You get a private yacht or catamaran with a skipper, a floating party with a sound system, a cooler full of cava, and a swim stop in the Mediterranean. Boats depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella Marina, or Cabopino, and you can tailor the itinerary to include dolphin spotting off the Strait of Gibraltar or a sunset cruise along the Costa del Sol. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day charter for a group of 12. Book through BoatHire24 and skip the stress.

Why Estepona for a hen do boat trip

Estepona is the quiet cousin of Marbella. It has a proper old town with cobbled streets and flower pots, not just a strip of designer shops. You can start your day with a walk through the Plaza de las Flores, then step onto a boat and leave the land behind. The water here is calmer than further east, because the coast curves and the winds are lighter. That means less seasickness and more time for dancing on the deck.

The town itself is a good base for a hen weekend because it has plenty of Airbnbs and hotels within walking distance of the port. You can do a boat trip, then hit a tapas bar in the old town without needing a taxi. If you want to make a full weekend of it, you can combine the boat with a visit to the Estepona old town or a day at the beach at Playa del Cristo.

For the actual boat charter, you are looking at motor yachts from 10 to 20 metres, catamarans with a trampoline net at the front, and RIBs if you want to go fast. Most charters include a skipper, fuel, and a basic sound system. You bring the decorations and the drinks. Some operators let you bring your own food, others offer a catering upgrade with paella or tapas.

Choosing the right boat for your group

The size of your group determines the boat type. For a hen do of 6 to 12 people, a motor yacht around 12 to 15 metres is the sweet spot. You get a saloon with air conditioning, a sun pad on the bow, and a sundeck at the stern. Catamarans are better for larger groups of 12 to 20 because they have more deck space and are more stable. If your hen is the type who likes speed, a RIB or speedboat can take you to the far side of the bay in 20 minutes, but you will not get the same lounging space.

Here is a quick comparison:

Boat typeMax guestsTypical lengthBest forPrice from (half day)
Motor yacht12-1412-16 mLuxury, comfort, sunbathingEUR 1,500
Catamaran12-2012-18 mStability, deck space, groupsEUR 2,000
RIB / speedboat6-107-9 mSpeed, dolphin watching, day tripsEUR 800
Sailing yacht8-1212-15 mClassic feel, quieter vibeEUR 1,200

Note that prices are rough guides. Actual quotes depend on the season, the boat model, and the extras you add. Always ask for a detailed quote before booking.

You can browse all available options on the BoatHire24 search page and filter by guest count and budget.

Itinerary ideas for your hen do boat Estepona

A typical half-day charter lasts four hours. You can do a morning trip from 10am to 2pm, an afternoon from 2pm to 6pm, or a sunset from 6pm to 10pm. The sunset slot is popular for hens because the light is golden and you get the sky turning pink over the water.

Option one: the classic coast cruise. Leave from Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina, head west past the sand dunes of Cabopino and the rock of Cala del Faro. Stop for a swim at a quiet cove near Estepona, then turn back. This route takes you past the Marbella Club Hotel and the Golden Mile, so you can wave at the mansions.

Option two: the dolphin safari. Head south towards the Strait of Gibraltar. The waters off Estepona and Sotogrande are a feeding ground for striped dolphins and common dolphins. You are almost guaranteed a sighting from May to October. The skipper will know the spots. You can combine this with a stop at the island of Isla de las Palomas or a swim off the coast of Sotogrande.

Option three: the sunset party. Depart at 6pm, cruise east towards Marbella, anchor off the coast of Cabopino, and watch the sun drop behind La Concha mountain. The crew can set up a Bluetooth speaker and you can drink cava while the sky changes colour. This is a good option if you want to go out for dinner afterwards in Puerto Banús.

For a full day (8 hours), you can go as far as the Nerja caves or the Costa Tropical, but that means a lot of time on the water. Most hen groups prefer to stay local and maximise the party time.

What to bring and what to expect

You need to bring your own drinks and food unless you arrange a catering package. Most boats have a cooler with ice, but check ahead. Bring plastic cups, not glass, because glass breaks and the skipper will not be happy. Decorations are fine as long as they are not heavy or messy. Bunting, balloons, and a banner with the hen's name are standard. Just avoid confetti or glitter that can go overboard.

Clothing: swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (factor 50, the Spanish sun is brutal), a hat, and a light cover-up for the wind. Even in summer, the sea breeze can feel cool when the boat is moving. Bring a waterproof phone case if you want to take photos on the swim stop.

Expect the skipper to give a safety briefing at the start. He will tell you where the life jackets are and what to do in case of emergency. Do not ignore it. The skipper is also your guide and can recommend good anchor spots. Do not try to bribe him to go faster or to a different area unless you have agreed it beforehand. These are professional skippers who know the coast and the regulations.

You are allowed to play your own music. Most boats have a Bluetooth or AUX connection. Make a playlist beforehand because the signal can be patchy offshore. If you want a DJ, some operators offer that as an extra, but it costs more.

Cost breakdown and booking tips

Prices vary widely depending on the season, the boat, and the extras. A half-day charter for a motor yacht in June starts from around EUR 1,500 for 12 people. That works out at EUR 125 per person, which is cheaper than a night out in Marbella. Catamarans are more expensive because they are bigger and more stable. RIBs are cheaper but less comfortable for lounging.

Extras that add to the cost: catering (around EUR 30-50 per person for tapas or paella), drinks packages (EUR 15-25 per person for cava, beer, soft drinks), water toys (paddleboard, kayak, inflatable float), and transport to the port if you are staying inland. Some operators charge a cleaning fee if you leave the boat in a state, so be tidy.

Booking tips: book at least two weeks in advance for June to September. For a hen do on a Saturday, book a month ahead. Always confirm the maximum guest number including the skipper. Most boats have a legal limit that includes the crew, so if the limit is 12, that means 11 guests plus 1 skipper. Ask for a written confirmation of the itinerary and the cancellation policy. Some operators offer a full refund if you cancel 72 hours before, others are stricter.

To see all available boats and compare prices, go to the BoatHire24 search page and filter by Estepona or Puerto Banús. You can read reviews from previous hen groups there.

Ports and departure points near Estepona

Estepona has its own marina, Puerto Deportivo de Estepona, which is small but functional. It has a few restaurants and a chiringuito. Most of the larger charter boats operate out of Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina, which are about 15-20 minutes drive east. Cabopino is another option, smaller and quieter, about 10 minutes west of Marbella.

If you are staying in Estepona town, the drive to Puerto Banús is about 15 minutes along the A-7 motorway. Taxis cost around EUR 20-25 each way. Some operators offer a transfer service for groups, so ask about that when you book. Sotogrande port is further west, about 20 minutes from Estepona, and is a good option if you want a more exclusive, less crowded departure point.

Benalmádena is further east, about 30 minutes from Estepona, and has a large marina with many charter options. It is a good backup if Estepona and Puerto Banús are fully booked.

For a hen do, Puerto Banús is the most convenient because it has parking, bars, and restaurants right at the port. You can step off the boat and go straight to a club or a steakhouse. But if you want a quieter start, Estepona port is fine.

Weather and best time to go

The Costa del Sol has over 300 sunny days a year, so the weather is rarely a problem. The best months for a hen do boat trip are May to October. June and September are ideal because the water is warm (22-24 degrees C) and the crowds are smaller than in July and August. July and August are hot (30-35 degrees C) and busy, but the sea is at its warmest (25-26 degrees C).

Wind is the main factor. The Levante wind blows from the east and can create choppy conditions, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar. The Poniente wind from the west is lighter and better for boating. Your skipper will know the forecast and may adjust the route to avoid the worst of it. If the wind is too strong, the skipper has the right to cancel for safety. Most operators will reschedule or refund in that case.

In spring (April-May) and autumn (October), the weather is still good but the water is cooler. You can still swim, but you might want a wetsuit. Winter trips are possible for a sunset cruise with blankets and mulled wine, but swimming is off the cards.

Common questions

Can we bring our own decorations? Yes, as long as they are not heavy or messy. Avoid confetti and glitter. Bunting and balloons are fine.

Is the skipper included? Yes, every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper. You do not need a boat licence.

What happens if it rains? Most operators will reschedule or offer a refund if the weather is bad enough to cancel. Check the policy before booking.

Can we play our own music? Yes, most boats have a Bluetooth or AUX connection. Make a playlist beforehand.

How far in advance should we book? At least two weeks for summer weekends. A month ahead is safer for a large group.

Can we bring children? Yes, but check with the operator. Some boats have age limits for safety reasons.

Is food included? No, unless you arrange a catering package. You can bring your own food and drinks.

What is the cancellation policy? It varies by operator. Most offer a full refund if you cancel 72 hours before. Always read the terms.

Can we choose the itinerary? Yes, within reason. The skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences. You can request a dolphin spot or a swim stop.

How much does it cost? From around EUR 1,500 for a half-day motor yacht for 12 people. Catamarans and full-day charters are more. Get a quote for your specific group size and date.

How to handle the hen do admin on the day

Organising a group of 12 to 20 people on a boat can feel like herding cats, but a little planning saves the chaos. Appoint one person as the group contact who communicates with the skipper. That person collects the money beforehand, confirms the meeting time, and keeps the group chat updated. The skipper does not want to chase down 15 separate people for payment or instructions.

Set a clear meeting point at the port, like the main fountain in Puerto Banús or the flagpole at Estepona port. Share the exact location in the group chat with a photo. Tell everyone to arrive 15 minutes early. The boat will not wait, and the skipper will charge you for the time if you are late. Bring a printed or digital copy of the booking confirmation and the skipper's phone number in case anyone gets lost.

If you are bringing a cake or a special surprise for the hen, tell the skipper in advance. He can help you store it in the galley fridge. Do not bring anything that needs to be kept frozen, because boat fridges are small and the ice will melt by hour three. A simple tray of cupcakes or a small cake works better than a full tiered sponge.

Where to eat and drink after the boat trip in Estepona

The boat trip ends, but the hen do does not. Estepona old town has a cluster of tapas bars on Calle Caridad and Calle Terraza that are walking distance from the port. Try Bar El Paseo for fried fish and a noisy atmosphere, or La Escollera on the seafront for grilled sardines and a view of the boats. If you want a sit-down dinner, book a table at Mesón El Madroño for traditional Spanish food or at La Casa del Rey for a more modern menu with a terrace.

For a post-boat party, head to the port area of Estepona where there are a few cocktail bars like La Plage and Mosh. They stay open late and are used to groups. If you want to go big, take a taxi to Puerto Banús (15 minutes) where the clubs like Pangea and La Suite are open until 6am. The taxi back to Estepona costs around EUR 25 and is easy to find at the rank outside the port.

If your group is staying in Marbella, the boat can drop you at Marbella Marina instead of Estepona. That puts you right next to the restaurants on the Golden Mile and the clubs in the centre. Coordinate this with the skipper when you book, because the itinerary and the fuel cost will change.

title: Stag Do Boat Estepona: Exciting Trips
excerpt: Planning a stag do in Estepona? A boat charter with a skipper is the ultimate way to celebrate. Think sun, sea, and a private party on the water.
metaDescription: Plan the ultimate stag do boat Estepona trip. Private charters with skipper, party packages, and dolphin spotting. Book your unforgettable bachelor party.
author: Mardo Soo
content:
The 30-second answer

For a stag do in Estepona, renting a private boat with a licensed skipper is your best bet. You get a floating party venue with no driving, no cleaning, and full control over the vibe. Expect to pay from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a decent motor yacht for eight people, including fuel and a skipper. You can add a DJ, a barbecue, or just anchor off a quiet cove with a cooler full of beer. Depart from Estepona Marina or nearby Puerto Banús, and you're minutes from the action.

Why Estepona for a stag do boat trip

Estepona is a solid choice for a stag do because it gives you the Costa del Sol party scene without the full-on chaos of Marbella or Puerto Banús. The old town is charming, the beaches are clean, and the marina has a decent selection of bars and restaurants. But the real draw is the sea. A stag do boat Estepona charter lets you escape the crowds and create your own private party. You can anchor at a secluded beach like Playa del Cristo, blast your own music, and swim in crystal-clear water. The weather is reliable from May to October, with average sea temperatures hitting 22-24 degrees C in summer. Plus, the Strait of Gibraltar is just a short cruise away, where you can spot dolphins and maybe even whales. It's a unique experience that beats a standard pub crawl hands down.

What to expect on a stag do boat rental

When you book a stag do boat Estepona charter, you get a private vessel with a skipper included. That means no one needs a boat licence, and you can focus on having fun. Most charters are for groups of 8 to 12 people, though larger yachts can handle up to 20 or more. The boat will have a sun deck, a shaded area, and a sound system. You can bring your own food and drink, or arrange catering. The skipper will handle navigation and safety, and can recommend the best spots for swimming, snorkeling, or just cruising. Typical itineraries include a trip along the coast to Puerto Banús to gawk at superyachts, or a run out to the open sea for dolphin watching. Half-day trips (4 hours) are popular, but full-day (8 hours) or sunset charters work well too. Prices start from around EUR 1,500 for a half-day on a motor yacht for eight, and go up to EUR 3,000-plus for a larger catamaran or a full-day package with extras.

Best boats for a stag do in Estepona

Not all boats are equal a stag party. You want something with space, a good sound system, and a bit of style. Motor yachts are the go-to: they're fast, stable, and have plenty of deck space. A 40-foot Azimut or similar can seat eight comfortably and hit 25 knots, so you can cover ground quickly. Catamarans are another option, they're more stable, have huge sun decks, and are great for larger groups. A Lagoon 42, for example, can handle 12 people and has a flybridge for panoramic views. RIBs and speedboats are cheaper and faster, but less comfortable for a long party. Fishing boats are a niche choice if the groom is into angling, but they lack the party vibe. For a proper stag do, stick with a motor yacht or a catamaran. Check out BoatHire24 for options in Estepona and nearby marinas.

Itinerary ideas for a stag do boat trip

A typical stag do boat Estepona charter starts from Estepona Marina. You head east towards Puerto Banús, passing the iconic La Concha mountain in the background. First stop: a swim at Cala del Faro, a quiet cove with clear water and rocky cliffs for jumping off. Then cruise into Puerto Banús to see the superyachts and maybe grab a drink at a waterfront bar (the skipper will wait). After that, head west towards the Strait of Gibraltar. This is where you're most likely to see dolphins, common, striped, and even bottlenose. If the group is up for it, you can go further to the Rock of Gibraltar for a photo op. For a full-day trip, include a barbecue lunch on board or stop at a beach club like Playa del Cristo. Sunset charters are also popular: watch the sun dip behind the mountains while sipping champagne. For more ideas, see our search page for itineraries and boat types.

What to bring and what to avoid

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50, you will burn), sunglasses, a hat, and a towel. Swimwear is a given. A cooler with drinks and snacks is fine, but check with the charter company if they provide ice. A Bluetooth speaker is redundant if the boat has a sound system, but bring a backup. Avoid glass bottles, most skippers ban them for safety. No illegal drugs, obviously. Keep the noise reasonable; the skipper can ask you to leave if you're causing trouble. Don't bring more people than the boat's capacity, it's a safety issue and the coast guard checks. And for the love of god, don't get so drunk that you fall overboard. The water is cold, and the skipper has to call the rescue services, which ruins the vibe for everyone.

How to book a stag do boat in Estepona

Booking is straightforward. Use a marketplace like BoatHire24 to compare boats, prices, and availability. Enter your group size, date, and port (Estepona, Puerto Banús, or Marbella). You'll get a list of options with photos and descriptions. Most charters require a deposit (typically 30-50%) and the balance on the day. Read the cancellation policy carefully, some are strict, others flexible. Ask about extras: a DJ, a photographer, catering, or a barbecue. Some companies offer party packages with decorations and a dedicated host. For a stag do, it's worth paying for a skipper who speaks English and knows the area. Book at least two weeks in advance in summer, as popular boats go fast. For more tips, check our blog on planning the perfect boat party.

Cost breakdown for a stag do boat Estepona

Prices vary by boat size, duration, and season. Here's a rough guide for a half-day (4 hours) charter for 8-10 people, including skipper and fuel:

Boat typePrice range (EUR)CapacityExtras
Motor yacht (40-50 ft)1,500 - 2,5008-12DJ, BBQ, drinks
Catamaran (40-50 ft)2,000 - 3,50010-16Stable, large sun deck
RIB/speedboat800 - 1,2006-8Fast, less space
Fishing boat1,000 - 1,8006-10Fishing gear included

Full-day (8 hours) adds about 50-70% to the price. Sunset charters (2-3 hours) are cheaper, from around EUR 600 for a small boat. Always confirm what's included: fuel, water, ice, and sometimes a basic sound system. Food and drinks are usually extra. For a stag do, budget around EUR 200-300 per person for a full-day experience with all the trimmings.

Common questions

Do we need a boat licence? No, all charters include a licensed skipper who handles everything.

Can we bring our own alcohol? Yes, most companies allow it. Some charge a corkage fee for glass bottles.

What happens if the weather is bad? The skipper decides. If it's unsafe, you can reschedule or get a refund (check the policy).

Is there a toilet on board? Yes, all motor yachts and catamarans have a toilet. RIBs and small speedboats usually don't.

Can we swim in the sea? Yes, the skipper will anchor at a safe spot. Bring towels and snorkel gear.

How far in advance should we book? At least two weeks in summer, one week in other seasons. Popular boats go fast.

What if someone gets seasick? Bring motion sickness tablets (e.g., Dramamine). The waters near Estepona are usually calm, but the Strait can get choppy.

Why Estepona Marina beats Puerto Banús for a stag do

You might think Puerto Banús is the obvious choice for a stag do boat, but Estepona Marina has some clear advantages. First, it is less crowded, so you avoid the chaos of superyacht traffic and drunken tourists falling into the harbour. Second, parking is easier and cheaper, which matters when you have a minibus full of lads. Third, the marina itself has a more relaxed vibe with decent bars like La Escollera and El Puerto, perfect for a pre-boat beer without the EUR 15 cocktails. The departure point is also closer to the best swimming spots: Cala del Faro is only 15 minutes east, and Playa del Cristo is 10 minutes west. If you want a quieter start to the day, Estepona wins. For a stag do boat Estepona trip, you get the same sea and sun with less hassle. Just note that some larger yachts (over 50 feet) might prefer Puerto Banús due to deeper water, but for most groups, Estepona is ideal.

The best time of year for a stag do boat in Estepona

May to October is the sweet spot for a stag do boat Estepona charter. June, July, and August are peak season: sea temperatures hit 22-24 degrees C, and there are 10-11 hours of daylight. But you pay a premium, and the marinas are busier. September is the secret winner: the water is still warm (21-23 degrees C), the crowds thin out, and prices drop by 10-20%. May and October are cooler but still pleasant, with air temps around 20-25 degrees C. Avoid November to March unless you are hardcore: sea temps drop to 15-17 degrees C, and the wind can be unpredictable. The Levante wind (easterly) can kick up choppy seas, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar. For a stag do, you want calm conditions so you can swim and party without everyone turning green. Check the forecast a week before and have a backup date. The skipper will advise, but booking in shoulder season gives you more flexibility and lower costs.

Which boat type works best for different stag do styles

Not every stag do is the same, so match the boat to your group. For a lads' party focused on drinking and dancing, a 40-50 foot motor yacht like a Sunseeker or Azimut is perfect: fast, flashy, and with a decent sound system. You can anchor off Cabopino or Cala del Faro, blast reggaeton, and jump off the bow. For a more chilled vibe with a barbecue and swimming, a catamaran like a Lagoon 42 or Fountaine Pajot is better: stable, huge sun deck, and a flybridge for panoramic views. It handles 12-16 people easily. If the groom is into adrenaline, a RIB or speedboat (e.g., a 30-foot Ribeye) can hit 40 knots and take you dolphin spotting in the Strait, but it is cramped for a party. For a fishing-themed stag, a 35-foot fishing boat with rods and a cooler is a niche choice, but you can still drink and grill the catch. Avoid sailing yachts for a stag do: they heel over, are slower, and have limited deck space. Stick with power or catamarans for maximum fun.

How to handle seasickness on a stag do boat trip

Seasickness can ruin a stag do boat Estepona charter faster than a hangover. The waters near Estepona are usually calm, but if you head towards the Strait of Gibraltar, the Atlantic swell can make things lumpy. Prevention is key: take motion sickness tablets like Dramamine or Stugeron an hour before departure. Avoid heavy food and alcohol until you are on the water. Ginger biscuits or chews help some people. If someone starts feeling rough, get them on deck in the fresh air, looking at the horizon, not down at the boat. The skipper can also anchor in a sheltered cove like Cala del Faro to let them recover. Do not let them stay below deck, it makes it worse. If the group is prone to seasickness, book a catamaran instead of a motor yacht: the twin hulls are much more stable. And skip the full-day trip if anyone is unsure, a half-day is safer. Worst case, the skipper will turn back early, but that kills the vibe for everyone.

What to do after the boat trip in Estepona

A stag do boat Estepona charter usually finishes back at the marina, and the party does not have to stop. Estepona old town is a 10-minute walk from the marina and has a great selection of bars and restaurants. Try Calle Terraza for tapas and drinks, or Calle Caridad for more lively spots. For a proper night out, head to Puerto Banús (15 minutes by taxi), where you have clubs like Pangea and Ocean Club, but expect EUR 20 cover charges and EUR 15 drinks. If the group is knackered, a beachfront restaurant like La Sal or El Pescador offers fresh seafood and a relaxed atmosphere. For a budget option, hit the chiringuitos on Playa del Cristo for grilled sardines and cold beer. If you want to extend the stag do, book a villa or apartment in Estepona rather than Marbella: it is cheaper, quieter, and closer to the marina. Check our search page for accommodation near the departure ports.

Legal and safety tips for a stag do boat in Spain

Spanish maritime law is strict, and the skipper is responsible for everyone on board. Do not bring illegal drugs: the coast guard does random checks, and you can be fined or arrested. Alcohol is fine, but the skipper can cut you off if anyone gets out of control. Life jackets are mandatory for everyone on deck, especially when the boat is moving. The skipper will do a safety briefing at the start, pay attention. Do not jump off the boat in busy channels or near other vessels. If someone falls overboard, the skipper will stop and call the rescue services, which can cost you EUR 500-1,000 for the emergency response. Keep the music at a reasonable level near other boats and residential areas. The capacity limit is not a suggestion: exceeding it invalidates the insurance and can get the charter cancelled. For a stag do boat Estepona trip, respect the rules and everyone has a good time. If you want more details, read our blog on boat safety in Spain.

How to save money on a stag do boat in Estepona

A stag do boat Estepona charter does not have to break the bank. Book in May, June, or September to avoid peak July-August prices. Half-day trips (4 hours) are cheaper than full-day, and you can always add a sunset extension. Choose a motor yacht over a catamaran: catamarans cost 30-50% more for the same capacity. Bring your own food and drink instead of buying onboard packages: a cooler with beer, wine, and sandwiches saves EUR 50-100 per person. Skip extras like a DJ or photographer, just use a Bluetooth speaker and someone's phone. Split the cost evenly among the group, but collect the money upfront to avoid awkward chasing. For a group of 10, a half-day motor yacht at EUR 1,800 works out to EUR 180 per person, which is cheaper than a night out in Puerto Banús. title: New Year's Eve Boat Party Marbella: Celebration Guide
excerpt: Ring in the new year on the water with a New Year's Eve boat party Marbella. This guide covers everything from fireworks views and champagne toks to booking tips and what to wear.
metaDescription: Plan a New Year's Eve boat party Marbella with fireworks, champagne, and skipper. Compare yachts, ports, and prices. Book your celebration today.
author: Andra Kiirkivi
content:
The 30-second answer

A New Year's Eve boat party Marbella is the best way to dodge the overcrowded clubs and overpriced restaurants. You get front-row seats to the fireworks over Puerto Banús, unlimited champagne (if you bring it), and a licensed skipper who handles the navigation. Expect to pay from around EUR 1,500 for a small motor yacht up to EUR 10,000 for a superyacht. Book at least three weeks in advance. The best ports are Puerto Banús for the big show and Marbella Marina for a quieter vibe.

Why choose a boat for New Year's Eve

You have probably done the whole thing before: queuing for an hour to get into a club, paying EUR 50 for a warm glass of cava, and then fighting for a taxi at 2am. A New Year's Eve boat party Marbella eliminates all of that. You are on your own private vessel with a small group of friends or family. The skipper takes care of the anchor and the safety. You just bring the drinks and the snacks. The boat becomes your floating VIP lounge. You can play your own music, eat your own food, and watch the fireworks from a perfect angle on the water. No one elbows you. No one spills beer on your shoes. The sea is calm in the bay, and the temperature rarely drops below 12 degrees C, so you can stay on deck with a coat and a blanket. It is a proper grown-up way to celebrate, and it costs less than a table at a top club when you split it six ways.

The best ports for New Year's Eve fireworks

Marbella has several departure ports, but not all of them offer the same fireworks experience. Puerto Banús is the main event. The harbour puts on a 15-minute firework display at midnight, and the boats pack into the marina basin. You see the bursts right above the luxury yachts and the La Concha mountain silhouette. The atmosphere is loud and flashy. Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo) has a smaller, more family-friendly display. It is less crowded, and you can anchor just outside the breakwater for a clear view. Cabopino and Estepona tend to have quieter celebrations, with local restaurants hosting their own parties. If you want dolphins and a sunset cruise before the countdown, go from Sotogrande or Benalmádena. Benalmádena has a big firework show at the marina, but it is a 40-minute drive from Marbella. For the best balance of spectacle and convenience, stick with Puerto Banús or Marbella Marina.

Types of boats for your party

Your choice of boat depends on your group size and your budget. For a group of 6 to 10 people, a motor yacht from around 12 to 15 metres works well. You get a saloon with a sound system, a flybridge for the views, and a galley for your food. Examples include the Azimut 55 or Sunseeker Predator 57. Prices start from EUR 1,500 for four hours. For a larger group of 12 to 20, a catamaran is the smart pick. Catamarans have a wide deck, a trampoline net at the bow, and a stable ride. You can dance on the deck without feeling seasick. A Lagoon 450 or Fountaine Pajot will cost from around EUR 3,000 for the evening. For the ultimate luxury, a superyacht over 20 metres with a crew and a DJ can run EUR 8,000 to EUR 15,000. If you want something faster and more casual, a RIB or speedboat works for a group of 6, but you will be cold and cramped. Stick to the bigger boats for comfort. All charters on BoatHire24 include a licensed skipper, so you do not need a boat licence.

What to bring and what to wear

The boat will have a sound system, a fridge, and sometimes a grill. You bring everything else. Make a playlist in advance, because the boat's Bluetooth connection can be flaky. Bring champagne, beer, wine, and mixers. Ice is essential, so buy a few bags from a supermarket. For food, think finger food: sandwiches, olives, nuts, cheese, and fruit. Avoid anything that melts or crumbles easily. You can order a catering platter from a local deli for around EUR 100 for 10 people. Wear layers. The evening starts warm, but once the sun sets, the temperature drops to 10-12 degrees C. A thick coat, scarf, and gloves are smart. Shoes should have flat soles and non-slip grips. Heels are a hazard on a wet deck. Bring a blanket for sitting on the flybridge. The skipper will have a basic first aid kit, but bring your own seasickness tablets if you are prone. The sea is usually calm in the bay, but it can get choppy near the Strait of Gibraltar. If you plan to anchor near Puerto Banús, arrive early to get a good spot. The marina fills up fast.

How to book and what to check

Booking a New Year's Eve boat party Marbella requires planning. Start by checking availability on the search page. Most boats are booked by mid-December. You should book at least three weeks in advance. When you contact the owner, ask these questions: What time does the charter start and end? Most New Year's charters run from 9pm to 1am or 10pm to 2am. Is the fireworks display visible from the anchor spot? Some boats stay in the marina, others go out to sea. If you want to see the fireworks from the water, confirm that the skipper will anchor near the display. What is the cancellation policy? Bad weather can cancel a charter in December. Make sure you get a full refund if the skipper calls it off. Does the boat have heating? Many motor yachts have cabin heating, but catamarans and sailing yachts often do not. Is the toilet working and accessible? Nothing ruins a party like a blocked marine head. What is included in the price? Some charters include a welcome drink, others include nothing. Always clarify. The price usually includes the skipper, fuel, and the boat. Extras like food, drinks, and decorations cost extra.

Costs and budgeting

The cost of a New Year's Eve boat party Marbella varies wildly. A small motor yacht for 6 people starts at around EUR 1,500 for four hours. A mid-size catamaran for 12 people is around EUR 3,000 to EUR 4,500. A superyacht with a crew and a DJ can hit EUR 12,000 or more. On top of the charter fee, budget for food and drinks. A supermarket run for 10 people costs about EUR 150. Catering from a local company costs EUR 200 to EUR 400. If you want decorations like balloons, banners, and tableware, add another EUR 50. Tipping the skipper is customary, usually 10 to 15 percent of the charter fee. Some owners ask for a security deposit of EUR 500 to EUR 1,000, which is refunded if you do not damage anything. Always get a written contract and pay by credit card or bank transfer for protection. Do not pay cash to a random person on the dock. Use a reputable marketplace like BoatHire24 to compare boats and read reviews from previous renters.

Local alternatives and insider tips

If you want a different vibe, consider a sunset cruise on December 30 and then a dinner in Estepona old town. The old town has a beautiful square with a Christmas market and a midnight countdown with free cava. For a more adventurous option, take a boat from Sotogrande and cruise towards the Strait of Gibraltar. You might see dolphins, and the views of Africa are clear on a good day. But the fireworks in Sotogrande are small. For the best Instagram shot, position your boat at the entrance of Puerto Banús marina, with the fireworks behind the superyachts. The skipper will know the exact spot. If you want to avoid the crowds entirely, book a charter from Cabopino and anchor near the dunes. You will see the distant lights of Marbella but no fireworks. That is fine if you just want a quiet night with your group. One more insider tip: book a boat that allows you to stay overnight. Some motor yachts have cabins where you can sleep after the party. That saves you the taxi hassle. Check the listing details on our blog for more specific recommendations.

Common questions

Can I bring my own alcohol on a New Year's Eve boat party Marbella?

Yes, you can bring your own alcohol. Most charters allow you to bring your own drinks and food. Some owners might charge a corkage fee if you bring premium champagne, so check beforehand. The boat will have a fridge and ice, but bring extra ice in a cooler.

Do I need a boat licence to charter a boat for New Year's Eve?

No, you do not need a licence. Every charter on BoatHire24 includes a licensed skipper who handles the navigation, anchoring, and safety. You just relax and enjoy the party. The skipper will also know the best spots for fireworks viewing.

What happens if the weather is bad on New Year's Eve?

If the weather is bad, the skipper will cancel the charter for safety reasons. You should get a full refund or the option to reschedule. Always check the cancellation policy before booking. December can have windy days, but Marbella's bay is usually sheltered.

How many people can fit on a boat for a New Year's Eve party?

Boat capacity varies. A small motor yacht fits 6 to 10 guests. A catamaran fits 12 to 20 guests. A superyacht can hold 20 to 50 guests. The number includes you and your guests, not the crew. Check the specific boat's maximum capacity on the listing.

What time does a New Year's Eve boat party usually start and end?

Most charters run from 9pm to 1am or 10pm to 2am. Some offer a longer option from 8pm to 3am for an extra fee. You can also book a sunset cruise from 4pm to 8pm and then attend a land-based party. Confirm the timing with the owner.

Are children allowed on a New Year's Eve boat party?

Yes, children are allowed on most boats, but check with the owner. Some boats have age restrictions for safety reasons. Catamarans are more family-friendly than motor yachts because they have more deck space and are more stable. Bring life jackets for kids.

Can I decorate the boat for New Year's Eve?

Yes, you can decorate the boat with balloons, banners, and tableware. Avoid confetti because it leaves a mess and can damage the marine environment. Use reusable decorations. Check with the owner if they allow tape or adhesive on the surfaces. Some owners provide basic decorations.

Why Puerto Banús outperforms other ports for NYE fireworks

Puerto Banús is not just the most famous marina on the Costa del Sol; it is the only one that turns its entire harbour into a stage for New Year's Eve. The fireworks launch from the central pier, between the superyacht berths and the luxury boutiques. From a boat anchored inside the marina, you see the explosions reflected in the water and on the polished hulls of the multimillion-euro yachts. The sound bounces off the surrounding buildings, creating a surround-sound effect you do not get from the beach. The downside: you must arrive early. The marina allows a limited number of charter boats to anchor inside the breakwater. Book a slip or an anchorage spot at least two weeks in advance. If you anchor outside the marina, you still get a good view, but you miss the immersive experience. For a more intimate setting, Marbella Marina is better. The fireworks there are smaller, but the crowd is thinner and the boat traffic is lighter. You can anchor 50 metres from the breakwater and have the whole display to yourself.

The best boat type for a group of 8 to 12 people

For a group of 8 to 12, a catamaran is the practical choice. A Lagoon 42 or Fountaine Pajot Elba 45 offers a wide, stable deck that does not roll like a monohull. You can set up a buffet table on the aft deck, string fairy lights along the bimini, and dance on the trampoline at the bow. The saloon has a galley with a fridge, stove, and sink, so you can prepare hot food. The cabins below deck are useful for storing coats and bags. The flybridge on a catamaran is large enough for 10 people to sit and watch the fireworks. The cost for a catamaran on New Year's Eve is from around EUR 3,000 for four hours. That is EUR 250 per person for a group of 12, which is less than a mediocre dinner in Puerto Banús. If you want a faster, more glamorous option, a motor yacht like the Azimut 60 or Sunseeker Manhattan 65 offers a more enclosed saloon with a proper sound system. But the deck space is smaller, and the boat rocks more at anchor. For comfort and value, a catamaran wins.

How to handle the December weather on the water

December in Marbella is not cold by northern European standards, but it is not the Mediterranean summer either. The average daytime temperature is 16 to 18 degrees C, dropping to 10 to 12 degrees C after sunset. The sea temperature is around 15 degrees C, so falling overboard is a real risk that requires immediate action. The wind in the bay is usually light, but the Levante wind can pick up in the afternoon, making the sea choppy near the Strait of Gibraltar. To stay comfortable on deck, bring a windproof jacket, a fleece layer, and a wool hat. The boat's cabin will be warmer, but the best views are from the flybridge or the bow. Ask the owner if the boat has a cockpit enclosure or a heater. Some motor yachts have a diesel heater that keeps the saloon toasty. Catamarans rarely have heating, so you rely on the cabin insulation. If the boat has a grill, you can cook sausages or burgers to keep warm. The skipper will monitor the weather and may move to a sheltered anchorage if the wind picks up. Trust their judgment; they know the local conditions better than any app.

What to do if you miss the midnight fireworks entirely

If your boat charter is delayed or the fireworks are cancelled due to weather, you have backup options in Marbella. The Puerto Banús promenade has live music and street performers until 2am. The Marbella old town has a square with a large screen showing the countdown from Madrid. The Estepona old town has a similar setup with free cava at midnight. For a more spontaneous celebration, drive to Nerja (about an hour east) for their famous cave-based New Year's party, but that requires advance tickets. If you want to stay on the water without the fireworks, book a sunset cruise on December 30 instead. The sunset over La Concha mountain is spectacular, and the bay is quieter. You can anchor near the Cala del Faro and watch the lights of Marbella twinkle on. The cost for a sunset charter is lower, from around EUR 800 for a small motor yacht. That is a smart alternative if you want the boat experience without the NYE premium.

How to negotiate the best price for a NYE charter

New Year's Eve is a peak date, so owners know they can charge a premium. But you can still negotiate if you book early or late. If you book in October or early November, some owners offer a 10 to 15 percent discount for early payment. If you book in the last week of December and the boat is still available, you can offer a lower price, say 20 percent off the listed rate, because the owner would rather have something than nothing. Always ask if the price includes the skipper, fuel, and cleaning. Some owners add a cleaning fee of EUR 100 to EUR 200. Clarify if the deposit is refundable and under what conditions. If you are a repeat customer or a local resident, mention that to the owner. They might offer a loyalty discount. Use the search page to compare multiple boats and contact several owners at once. Do not accept the first price you see. A little haggling can save you EUR 300 to EUR 500, which pays for the champagne.
